frames.c: Mechanics check a wing hinge on an HX-4 Merlin in a coastal hangar at sunset, its tethered LR-1 rifle cradled beside it and still cabled to the capacitor pack. Only a dozen Merlins were built, and they proved a frame could fold into flight.

vehicles.c: An M9 Teamster stands watch at an alpine road tunnel in a midnight snowstorm while a truck and two tracked supply carriers file past its knees. More Teamsters serve than any other US frame, and the vehicles still do the hauling.

supers.c: A CX-1 Concord rides a heavy-lift pontoon through a canal lock in predawn rain, chained down with its weapons stowed. The 17 m escort frame on the dock reaches less than halfway up it. A dozen exist, and each one was built to be seen.

carriers.c: An AWX-1 Marlinspike drifts on a safety tether above the lunar far side, solar wings out, beside the warship whose catapult it was built for. It has no legs, and nobody yet knows how it should fight. By 2327 every carrier launches its descendants.

orgs.c: A house Rigger anchors to the torn truss of an abandoned station past the elevator and lifts out a greenhouse module that is still growing. Its two operators live in the doubled cab for a week at a time. The prospecting houses keep their own books, and claims like this one are what they settle by tether duel.

headline.c: Dawn at a dry river crossing in 2186. A sand-worn League industrial frame rests beside its supply carriers while crews and civilians get ready to move. Across the river a Kestrel waits by its battery pit, and the city behind them is burning.

fb1.c: An M4 Garrison crouches in a foothill motor pool, its M30 pointed at the ground and its pile bunker folded. From behind, the tank it grew out of is plain to see: the sloped glacis, the cupola head, the turbine louvres.

fh3.c: A Kestrel has just landed on a closed highway in the morning haze, knees still bent and dust settling. It carries its LR-3 and two missiles under each wing binder. The fans make no flame and no smoke.

xc1.c: Three Concords loom over a press stand on an airbase apron at dusk, more than twice the height of the frames parked beside them. The pilot pair stand on the chest walkway. It was meant to look like a triumph.

wS1.c: Four Garrisons ambush a tank column from a Zagros ravine in 2162. The lead frame fires a shoulder missile uphill. The tanks can't climb to where they stand.

wS7.c: At night on the Malan Bridge, the Choir kneels across the approach and holds one forearm over the crossing to catch shrapnel. Buses, handcarts and families keep moving beneath it. Its rifle stays slung.

wO1.c: Striking workers hold a pressure bulkhead aboard an orbital construction station in 2166. A four-armed AW-3 Lifter braces the structure with its upper arms and holds a rivet driver and a welding torch in its lower pair. Security waits beyond a sealed door.

c2.c: An armourer opens the stock of an LR-3 in a forward workshop to service the MHI capacitor inside. No tether runs to a power pack. Through the hangar door, a Kestrel's leg gives the rifle its scale.

q2.c: Night rain in a highway pit. An Osprey's crane arm lowers a fresh QX pack into the spine of a kneeling Kestrel, guided by crew on the catwalks. The whole swap takes about a minute and a half.

o14.c: A Pavise leads from a foggy ridge with its antenna panels open and its coilgun braced on a bipod. Two Hauberts follow it through the valley. Below, the enemy's headlights wander. You can't see the jamming, only what it does.

va22.c: Three Kafilas, turretless tank hulls packed with fuel drums, spares and shade cloth, halt at a desert rest stop at blue hour. Mechanics check tracks while a family takes on water. A Haboob stands guard far behind.

vc21.c: A Heron carries four QX packs on one sling pallet up an Afghan valley toward a forward pit, where an Osprey and a kneeling Kestrel wait.

yg22.c: A Safina, once a bucket-wheel mining crawler, rolls ahead of a sandstorm with its hangar doors open on a row of Haboobs. One frame walks down the ramp. The deck carries workshops, water treatment and a small refinery.

yh30.c: The only Rookery holds station over a cloud deck at dawn on its four ducted fans, well away from any fighting. A Harrier is secured on the service deck beside a crane and a battery pack.

sfe0.c: An armed station tug escorts a civilian tender past a construction ring in 2186. Its weapons are a rivet gun and a cutting rig bolted to its truss. A tethered worker on the hull gives the scale.

og_mhi.c: In Mitsurugi's coastal works, technicians hand-calibrate an unarmed Kizuna's fingers from a gantry. In the next bay, the capacitors that Mitsurugi sells abroad roll past on carts.

ac05.c: Gloria Abernathy defends her swap pit near Shindand during the Hari River Offensive. Her Osprey's crane arm keeps a pack steady in its socket while the other hand aims an M30 over the berm. Her crew shelter in the revetments beside a kneeling Kestrel.

QAC.c: Delegates, engineers and repair crews argue around a plain table in a shaded Khartoum courtyard in 2186. Outside, the depot keeps working: a League frame, Kafila carriers and the water queue.

UNEL.c: Projected. A lunar yard turned relief port after the war. Suited crews pass medical and rebuilding cargo through pressure locks while people inside watch a convoy leave for Earth.

wS5.c: The Great Sand Sea at dusk in 2183. Three sets of supply tracks meet at a wrecked depot among burnt-out hulls, and one Sirocco still works there. The Jinn is nowhere in sight.

fn1.c: An NK-12 stands knee-deep at an Indian field station in monsoon rain. Engineers check the cooling plumbing behind its big radiator grilles and rubber joint boots. Nashik rebuilt that cooling system twice before Moscow agreed it needed rebuilding.

fg3.c: During an evacuation drill outside Tunis, an Elissa kneels behind its rescue shield. Medics load a stretcher into one of the four pods racked behind its hips.

ac26.c: Hawa Abdelrahman's Sirocco faces the Jinn in the Great Sand Sea, the second time they meet. The Jinn stands more than twice its height. This time she lowers her gun.

xb1.c: In a cold Canadian hangar, the Aurora's upper half hangs on crane slings above its legs, two metres short of the waist ring. Calgary built the legs and Montreal the torso. When Canada splits, the halves end up on opposite sides of the line.

yg51.c: Projected. Inside a Hospital Safina well behind the North African Front, the old mech bays hold quiet wards. Behind a screen, the graft vats work.

yh51.c: Projected. The Hakobune rises on its fans over a storm-damaged Japanese coast. Two Kizunas wait in its open rescue hangar. It carries no weapons.

og_tng.h: Everyone eats at the same table
og_tng.c: Projected. The Tangier collective shares one long meal in the shipbreaking yard, mechanics and volunteers together. The half-built Tramuntana stands behind them, its curved hull ribs already part of its body.

xq1.c: Projected. The Tramuntana stands guard on a Tangier quay while families board the ferries across the strait.

wO8.h: Survey camp, according to the manifest
wO8.c: Melas Chasma, 2186. A small camp in Ascension's old livery digs a careful trench at the old ████████ site, dwarfed by the canyon wall. On paper it is a survey.

xl1.c: At the south-pole yard, the crews build their own Custodian on a slipway between two half-finished ships from different blocs. Its armour is patched from all of them, every insignia ground off.

o9.c: 2186. Company depot open day: the Concord's pilot pair climb while recruits pass through implant screening. One recruit is quietly led aside.

wW14.c: 2186. At Malapert, Union and British crews join the first keel section of Britain's orbital hull.

o39.c: 2186. The network moves a train of frames on schedule. Beyond its lights, steppe crews watch the crossing.

xk3.c: 2180s. At Nashik, pilots return their augmentation harnesses to the shared rack; the transfer capsule remains unopened.

o46.c: 2186. A Harmattan shelters a water point from the haboob, supplying water and medical care in its lee.

wS14.c: 2177. White-painted donated frames escort food through the Copperbelt as a League checkpoint lets them pass.

wO18.c: 2182. On the drowned Gulf coast, applicants bring the skills and equipment that might sustain a settlement on Mars.

wO22.c: 2186. Judges and river officers hear both banks at one table beside the shrinking Rio Bravo.

wO20.c: Projected war. Beneath Strasbourg, the ethics panel keeps reading; one member looks up at the map of Mars.

wO6.c: 2186. Three generations keep the family tender's records, knowledge and continuity contract in the asteroid belt.

xm9.c: 2186. At an oasis, keepers treat the Jinn and patients while distant watchers study the culture vats.

wE15.c: Projected war. At Vladivostok, envoys bless the departing pilots and engineers beneath the rescue ark.

wW17.c: Projected war. Refugees cross the Arctic sea ice toward the Hearth; the distant sun is only a pale band.

frames.label: Frames
frames.intro: The frame took war back to where it started: humanoid wrestling humanoid in the dust. Strip away the reactors, the linear rifles and the wing binders, and what's left is two bodies trying to bring each other down, each one flown by whoever has the strength to do it. Select a frame to see what powers it, what it carries and the doctrine it was built for.
turns: There were no mechs yet, only the industries that would build them. Halcyon made jets, Brannock-Hale tanks, Tianlong excavators and Mitsurugi rescue robots, and logging crews walked hydraulic rigs up hillsides. Every frame since has borrowed its parts from one of them.

Brannock-Hale put a construction walker's legs under a tank's armour, and the M4 was slow, loud and very hard to kill. Halcyon, VEK, Boreal and the League's workshops all licensed or rebuilt it, while Tianlong went its own way with the Tieniu. A dozen hand-built Merlins proved a frame could fly.

The blocs stopped borrowing and built for their own wars. The Kestrel cut transformation to two seconds and ran on swap batteries. The Tieshan went the other way: simple, armoured and built in thousands. The Haubert took any role overnight on standard hardpoints. You could tell a bloc by its outline.

These frames answer what Gen 2 taught. The Harrier carries a laser to survive the anti-air rockets, the Bulwark holds the swap points Kestrels depend on, the Mamont opens the gaps, and the Pavise blinds before it shoots. Frames start coming from places nobody planned for: Nashik, Tunis and, by 2183, the Moon.

Every prototype is built around something the last generation couldn't do: a beam weapon, a reactor, beamed power, a network in place of a pilot, a sworn pair, no legs at all. Most exist in ones and twos, and nobody yet knows which of them is the future.
fams: Tanks with legs, built to be fixed with a wrench.
Modular knights, and hand-built frames for aces.
Fast frames from a workers' collective in a squatted hangar, with the drawings free to anyone who asks.
Cold-weather frames from a country that buys from both blocs.
Iron mountains, in their thousands, and lately the network that moves them.
Herder-mechanics' fast frames from the Darkhan rail sheds, joined late by Berlin's splinter.
Heavy, aggressive, and few. Built in Russia, and now in India.
OKB-7's Indian line, learning to build frames for sworn pilots.
Rescuers first, then the world's best actuators.
Three blocs' parts on one frame, until Khartoum starts designing its own.
French and Italian engineering on the Maghreb coast, and the Charter's second design office.
Built on the Moon for a gravity it doesn't have, and given to the UN.
Seen, photographed or recovered, and claimed by no maker. Designations are whatever the people who saw them wrote down.

nodes.t: Halcyon's jet lineage
nodes.x: Halcyon's fighter and ground-attack jets. The wing binders, avionics and flight-control software of every Halcyon frame descend from them.

nodes.t: First variable frame; transformed slowly
nodes.x: The first mech that could fold into a flight mode. Transformation took eleven seconds, and the tethered LR-1 had to be stowed first. Only a dozen were built, but they proved the idea.

nodes.t: Licensed Garrison, lightened for air drops
nodes.x: Halcyon's first mech was a licensed Brannock M4 Garrison with its armour cut back so a tiltrotor could carry it. The Army never forgave Halcyon for improving its design.

nodes.t: America's signature variable frame
nodes.x: The Merlin's flight mode on the Sparrowhawk's ground frame. Two-second transformation, a quick-swap battery spine driving electric ducted fans in the calf nacelles, and an LR-3 in hand. Its forty-minute endurance defined US doctrine.

nodes.t: Heavier strike Kestrel with point defence
nodes.x: A bigger Kestrel with QX-3 packs, more wing stores, and a PL-2 laser to survive the Pact's anti-air rockets and the Sapsans' missiles. Slightly slower to transform, much harder to shoot down. Svalbard turned it from an option into the standard.

nodes.t: Swap-pit support frame with battery crane
nodes.x: A non-transforming frame on the Sparrowhawk line, built to run swap pits: a battery crane on one arm, an M30 on the other, and Brannock hybrid power for endurance. Pit crews fight in them when the pit is attacked, which is often.

nodes.t: Harrier with a microwave power receiver
nodes.x: A Harrier with a dorsal rectenna for the SKYLINE beamed-power trials. Two exist. One has flown for six hours without landing.

nodes.t: Armour, fire control, crew survival
nodes.x: Brannock-Hale's tank business supplied the armour layout, fire control and crew-survival thinking for every frame it builds.

nodes.t: Legged demolition and logging rigs
nodes.x: Hydraulic legged rigs for demolition and logging on steep ground. The first machines to walk at this scale.

nodes.t: The first mech in combat service
nodes.x: A construction walker's legs under a tank's armour and fire control. Slow, loud and very hard to kill. Almost everyone has licensed, copied or rebuilt it.

nodes.t: Heavy frame that holds swap points
nodes.x: Extra armour and a second Hornet pod, built to seize and hold the swap points Kestrels depend on. The Army calls it the frame that keeps the Air Force flying, and says so often.

nodes.t: The US Army's workhorse
nodes.x: The Garrison redesigned for fire teams: hybrid power that lets it go quiet in ambush, standard Hornet mounts, and a stake driver on the left arm. More Teamsters serve than any other US frame.

nodes.t: Testbed for the turbine-capacitor plant
nodes.x: A Teamster rebuilt around a frame-sized HT-20 plant and the AR-40E electrothermal rifle: the Army's attempt to match linear-weapon penetration without depending on Halcyon.

nodes.t: Sensor masts and quiet hulls
nodes.x: European wheeled reconnaissance vehicles, whose sensor masts and quiet running shaped VEK's priorities.

nodes.t: Licensed Garrison with VEK sensors
nodes.x: A licence-built M4 Garrison with a VEK sensor head and a submarine-derived fuel cell in place of the turbine. Quieter and sharper-eyed than the original, and the first mono-eye frame.

nodes.t: The standard-hardpoint modular frame
nodes.x: VEK's first clean-sheet design, built around the standard hardpoint and BZ-4 stacks. Rounded knightly armour, a mono-eye on a track, and one frame reconfigured overnight for any role.

nodes.t: Lance knight of the hunter-killer lance
nodes.x: A heavier Haubert built to close and finish: reinforced arms for the HEAT lance, a large shield, and BZ-6 reformer stacks so it can refuel from any truck.

nodes.t: EW and coilgun sniper frame
nodes.x: Carries the Spiegel coilgun, the Union's best EW suite and Fenrir missiles. It leads formations under Directive 5 and takes the kill shot under Directive 8.

nodes.t: Hand-built ace frame on Haubert bones
nodes.x: Castellani's take on the Haubert: lighter armour, Stack-R racing cells and hand-tuned actuators. Each one is built for one named ace and painted red and gold.

nodes.t: Plasma-blade prototype for the top ace
nodes.x: Built around the Lama Ardente plasma blade, with Destrier-style arm bracing and a licensed capacitor core in the chest. It fights at full power for about forty seconds.

nodes.t: The Blitz's heir, built in a squatted hangar
nodes.x: Funkenwerk's first frame, from people who thought the Haubert's knight armour was a costume. It is a light runner on a modular cell stack, lighter than an Écuyer and faster than anything else the Union fields on the ground, assembled in open bays at Tempelhof where anyone can walk in and watch. Crews paint their own frames, so no two match. The drawings are public, so a field workshop can fix one with whatever fits. The German and Dutch contingents bought it to screen their columns. Union staff officers called it unprofessional, and Funkenwerk printed that on its posters.

nodes.t: Open-drawing raider that hunts jammers
nodes.x: German for a ricochet, and for someone who won't fall in line. After Svalbard, six collectives in Berlin, Leipzig, Rotterdam, Gdańsk, Lisbon and Marseille built it from one set of public drawings. It runs on a reformer stack that makes its own hydrogen from diesel, so it never waits on a depot the way the Blitz did. Its Fenrir missiles home on jammers, and a pirate-radio rig in the back drowns out everyone else's signals. The Union has never ordered one. Its contingents have more than a hundred.

nodes.t: The punks grown up: black, sealed and fast
nodes.x: Funkenwerk's first frame built to a state contract, and the one that split the cooperative. When the Union procurement office stalled for a third year, Berlin offered to pay directly, and the members voted 61 to 39 to take the money. The ones who left kept the Querschläger drawings. The ones who stayed built this: the Querschläger grown up, with a sealed, faceted hull, a reformer stack buffered by a licensed capacitor core, and a Spiegel coilgun it can fire on the run. Before it, no two Funkenwerk frames ever matched. Every Aufbruch is black. In Berlin that reads as a promise that Germany will stop waiting for the rest of the Union. In Paris it reads as a warning. Two are flying.

nodes.t: Rail sheds, rally trucks and herders' motorcycles
nodes.x: Darkhan's railway sheds, the Gobi's rally-truck garages and every herder who keeps a forty-year-old motorcycle running. Khiimori's frames come out of their habits: weld what you have, carry your own spares, and never trust a depot to be there.

nodes.t: Wild horse: a welded-tube runner from the Darkhan sheds
nodes.x: Named for the takhi, the wild horse of the steppe. Darkhan's rail workshops built it for outriders who were wearing out stripped Tieniu on the frame-train routes. It is a welded tube frame like a rally truck's, on long legs from a tracklayer's suspension, with a tractor's multi-fuel diesel and a felt-lined cab big enough to sleep in. The welds are ugly and it rattles at speed, but it is faster than anything else the Pact owns, and any herder's mechanic can fix it. Beijing never ordered one. The outriders bought them straight from the shed.

nodes.t: Eagle: the Takhi grown into a raider
nodes.x: Named for the golden eagles the steppe's hunters fly from the saddle. The Bürged is a Takhi grown into a raider: longer legs, a rocket rack on the back, a carbon blade, and a stooping charge the crews learned from watching the eagles. Its engineering is still Darkhan's: hand-bent tube, salvaged Tieshan actuators and a diesel tuned past what the manual allows. Outriders ride it a hundred kilometres between depots and fight with what they carry. Moscow's planners underestimate it every year.

nodes.t: “White Wind”: the splinter's answer to the Aufbruch
nodes.x: In 2185 the thirty-nine percent who walked out of Funkenwerk over the Berlin contract arrived at Khiimori's sheds with the Querschläger drawings and nowhere else to go. They had sworn never to paint a frame black. The Tsagaan Salkhi is what the two shops built that winter, its sealed armour painted matt white over dark joints, with blue khadag scarves at the shoulders: as unlike the Aufbruch as the splinter could make it. The outriders named it for the tsagaan zud, the white winter that kills a herd in a night. Berlin's sealed panels and reformer stack sit on Darkhan's long legs and stooping charge, and for the first time the welds are clean. The money did not come from a vote. Beijing pays for the machined parts and the shed time, and some of the thirty-nine percent bristle at having walked out on one state's contract only to take another's. It is the fastest frame anyone has built, low and swept back, and it looks like it wants to hurt you. Beijing asked for the drawings, and the collective published them the same week in Mongolian, Mandarin and German. Three are flying.

nodes.t: Arctic mining logistics
nodes.x: Tracked haulers and snow tractors that kept northern mines supplied across winter ice roads. Boreal's heated drivetrains, and its habit of wasting no heat at all, start here.

nodes.t: Licensed Garrison, winterised
nodes.x: Canada's first frames were Brannock M4 Garrisons built under licence in Calgary, with heated actuators, wide snowshoe feet and a turbine that would start at forty below. Washington set the licence terms; Ottawa paid them.

nodes.t: Arctic frame on US bones with a Union sensor head
nodes.x: Boreal's first own design: a Teamster-pattern chassis on snowshoe feet, a hybrid plant that can idle for a week on one tank of diesel, and a VEK sensor head, bought because Washington wouldn't export its newest one. US officers call it a Teamster for people who don't trust the US Army. Norway bought forty.

nodes.t: Runs as cold as the ice it hides in
nodes.x: Built after Svalbard, where the Union showed that whoever is seen first loses. The Wolverine can lie in the snow for days on a reformer-stack trickle, with an insulated hull and passive sensors, and its thermal signature is close to the ice around it. Its fuel cells are Union-pattern. So, increasingly, are its customers.

nodes.t: Sealed long-endurance frame for the high Arctic
nodes.x: Officially a search-and-rescue frame: a sealed cab two people can live in for a month, a heat-recovery loop that wastes almost nothing, and a power budget counted in watts rather than kilowatts. Boreal builds it in Calgary and Montreal, either side of a line nobody has drawn yet. The Halifax Motion passed the week it was unveiled, and Ottawa and Washington have argued about who owns it ever since. Its life-support loop will outlast the country that built it.

nodes.t: Diesel construction machinery
nodes.x: Tianlong's civilian excavators and tractors supplied the diesel-electric drive, the hydraulics and the factories.

nodes.t: “Iron Ox”: excavator drive, shoulder cannon
nodes.x: An excavator drive train in an egg-shaped armoured torso, with a tank gun on the shoulder that could only fire from a kneel. Thousands were built, and many still serve in the League.

nodes.t: “Iron Mountain”: the most-built mech in the world
nodes.x: Adopted the same year as the Type-09 cannon it was built to carry. Thick armour, few moving parts, a cockpit buried deep in the torso, and a multi-fuel diesel. Six weeks to train a pilot.

nodes.t: Depot upgrade: radios, optics, drum rifle
nodes.x: Tieshans upgraded at depot level with better radios, optics and Type-07 drum rifles, so older frames can be brought up to standard without new production lines. The new radios carry Tianshu's data link, which is the real upgrade.

nodes.t: “Light Mountain”: slab armour, long legs, drum rifle
nodes.x: A Tieshan built to keep up with the mountain regiments instead of kneeling for them. A second Tianlong line swapped the cast hull for flat welded slab armour, lengthened the legs and traded the long cannon for a Type-07 drum rifle, with a single rocket tube on the shoulder. It was taller and faster than the Tieshan, and it died faster too: slab plates split where the cast hull would have shrugged off the hit. The line closed after a few thousand were built, but the drum rifle it proved went into every Tieshan-Kai refit.

nodes.t: “Iron Wall”: fortress-belt and anti-air frame
nodes.x: A squat, heavily armoured Tieshan derivative built to be dug in, with a Type-09 cannon and anti-air rocket racks for the Air Umbrella. It barely walks and never retreats. Behind the belt, a salt reactor train feeds it by cable while its diesel idles.

nodes.t: “Sky Eye”: one pilot, a Tianshu node, six uncrewed frames
nodes.x: Beijing's answer to augmented pilots was to change the network, not the pilot. A Tieshan-Kai chassis carries a Tianshu node in the torso and an unaugmented pilot, who commands six uncrewed Tieshan conversions that walk wherever Tianshu sends them. The network proposes and the pilot approves. The same node runs the trial frame's Salt Core, so the pilot commands six frames and never touches the power. In trials the uncrewed frames hold a kneeling line better than conscripts do. Nobody has yet tested what happens when the link is jammed.

nodes.t: OKB-7's jet lineage
nodes.x: OKB-7's interceptors and long-range bombers. Its first frame took their landing gear, their twin cannon and their control laws, and it dropped from their bomb bays.

nodes.t: Airborne raider on interceptor landing gear
nodes.x: OKB-7's first frame, built for the Pact's airborne divisions and dropped by parachute platform from converted bombers. Its legs are interceptor landing-gear forgings: long oleo struts that soak up a hard landing and give it a loping run no Tieniu could match. Its control laws came straight from the Strizh with the limits left off, which suits a fighter pilot in a g-suit. A Korsak pilot has no g-suit. At Talysh the drop scattered across the passes, and several frames were recovered with their pilots unconscious in the seat. Fewer than ninety were built before the airborne divisions went back to light tanks. OKB-7 kept the control laws on file. The Rys flew them again, and the Volk is what they became once Department Zero had pilots who could take them.

nodes.t: Enlarged Tieshan chassis, built-in guns
nodes.x: OKB-7 enlarged the Tieshan chassis, fitted twin diesels, built a rotary cannon into each forearm and added a Grad-M battery. The Pact's first frame built for quality over numbers. Since the Delhi Accession, a second OKB-7 line at Nashik builds them too.

nodes.t: Breakthrough heavy with integral maul arm
nodes.x: The breakthrough frame: an enormous articulated right-arm steel maul, a left forearm rotary, a Grad-M battery and armour that shrugs off rifle fire. It breaks the barriers the waves behind it pour through.

nodes.t: Elite rail frame for augmented pilots
nodes.x: A lighter, faster Medved derivative with a Type-12 rail rifle and a KN-1 capacitor. Its control system assumes an augmented pilot; ordinary pilots black out in it. Beijing has never fielded one.

nodes.t: Siege frame: Kalibr-305 or Iskra
nodes.x: The heaviest conventional frame ever built. It anchors itself with spades and fires the Kalibr-305, or carries the Iskra particle cannon fed by cable from an MTU-7 truck.

nodes.t: Fission-powered test frame
nodes.x: A Mamont chassis carrying the Pamir micro-reactor. It can run for weeks. Its pilots' radiation exposure is a state secret: ███ mSv per sortie. Test pilots assigned: ██. Still flying: █.

nodes.t: India's licence-production tradition
nodes.x: Decades of Indian factories building foreign fighters and tanks under licence, and learning more from each contract than the licensor meant to teach.

nodes.t: OKB-7's heavy frame, rebuilt for heat and monsoon
nodes.x: The price of the Delhi Accession: Medveds built at Nashik under OKB-7 supervision, with sealed joints for the monsoon, larger radiators for the plains, and Indian crews for the breakthrough groups. Nashik's engineers rebuilt the cooling system twice before Moscow agreed it needed rebuilding.

nodes.t: Paired frames for oath-sworn pilots
nodes.x: Nashik's first clean-sheet design, built around the Nashik Oath rather than Department Zero: two lighter, Volk-derived frames that fight as a sworn pair, linked so that each pilot sees what the other sees. The augmentation is worn, not implanted: a pilot rig that comes off and goes back to the unit store. The Ashvins are the twin divine horsemen of the old stories. Moscow wants the pair for the breakthrough groups; their pilots want them for the line.

nodes.t: Bought from the rival, maintained on its schedule
nodes.x: In 2173, after a decade of raids it couldn't answer and a ridge it had to give up, Delhi bought the only frames anyone would sell it quickly: export Tieshans from Tianlong, the same model that had knelt above the Ladakh pass. Indian depots added bigger radiators and a second radio. Everything else came from China, and spares came only through Tianlong's export depots, released when Tianshu scheduled them. Indian crews learned more from the Tieshan than Tianlong meant to teach. They also learned what it is to wait for a Chinese network to decide when your frame can walk. In 2186, a week after the Sealed Session, the schedule stopped.

nodes.t: Japanese disaster robotics
nodes.x: Decades of Japanese work on rescue robots and powered exoskeletons, the origin of Mitsurugi's lead in actuators and balance control.

nodes.t: Unarmed disaster-response frame
nodes.x: An unarmed rescue frame for earthquakes and tsunamis, with the best balance control and hands in the world. The Japanese public met mechs as rescuers first.

nodes.t: JSDF coastal-defence frame
nodes.x: A clean humanoid frame for coast and island defence, with hybrid cells, a Type-L coil carbine and an HF-1 sonic blade. Understated outside, superb actuators inside.

nodes.t: Upgraded Hayate for live test units
nodes.x: A Hayate with spare power and mounts for whatever prototype the lab sends next. The live test units fly them.

nodes.t: First frame built around a beam weapon
nodes.x: A Shiden rebuilt around one weapon, and lopsided because of it: a braced right shoulder and forearm cradle for the BX-0 emitter, and a cooling module on the left of the back with thermal cartridges the ground crew swap between test strings. It's the first frame designed around an energy weapon rather than adapted to carry one, with a Mk.III core behind the right chest. Clean white with blue and red accents, and no crest. One exists, and every bloc's intelligence service knows where it is kept.

nodes.t: Rebuilt Garrisons and Tieniu
nodes.x: Surplus M4 Garrisons and Type-01 Tieniu rebuilt in League workshops with sand filters and whatever parts were available. Every League frame starts here.

nodes.t: Tieniu torso on Garrison legs
nodes.x: Qadira's first production frame: a licensed Tieniu torso on Garrison-pattern legs with wide desert feet. Ugly and reliable, and the League has stuck with that approach since.

nodes.t: Q-Mix turbine, VEK-pattern sensors
nodes.x: The current League frame: a Q-Mix turbine, second-hand VEK sensor heads, and mounts that take US or Eurasian pods. Every part has a supplier in at least two blocs.

nodes.t: Kestrel airframe, VEK sensors, MHI blade
nodes.x: Grey Lantern builds from bought and stolen parts: a Kestrel airframe with the transformation removed, a VEK sensor head, an MHI sonic blade. No two are alike, and none are legal.

nodes.t: Built in Khartoum to hold ground and shelter people
nodes.x: The first Qadira frame designed in Khartoum instead of assembled from three blocs' parts: a Sirocco chassis with a sealed cab, a dozer-blade shield wide enough to cover a family, water panniers and ground-level first-aid support, and a Q-Mix turbine re-tuned for local fuels. Its designers spent a month in the Great Sand Sea watching how the Jinn moves among people. It is the line the League will keep building after it stops being a league.

nodes.t: Building to European licence
nodes.x: Shipyards in Tunis and Bizerte and rail works in Algiers that built ferries, rolling stock and tractors under French and Italian licence for most of a century. Their engineers learned the European way of doing things, and kept the old Carthaginian habit of trading with everyone.

nodes.t: Haubert built in Tunis for the Union's partners
nodes.x: After the Maghreb Depot Strikes, Strasbourg promised its North African partners they would never again be left blind or stranded, and opened a Haubert line in Tunis to prove it: sealed joints, sand filters, a dust-shielded mono-eye track and a finish of sand and slate. French engineers ran the plant. Tunisian and Algerian crews built and flew the frames, and named them after the wind from the north.

nodes.t: Castellani's craft for desert lances
nodes.x: Castellani opened a workshop beside the Tunis line to build Falcos for the partner states' aces, then a cheaper frame for the rest of their lances: Falco-pattern actuators, BZ-6 stacks that refuel from any truck, and a tall sensor mast for the open desert. Its Tunisian pilots gave it the Italian name for the hot wind off the Sahara. The Italian engineers who came for three years have stayed for ten.

nodes.t: The Charter's first frame from Tunis
nodes.x: When the Maghreb signed the Khartoum Charter, the Tunis works went with it, and so did most of the French and Italian engineers who ran them. Under Qadira they are building a frame that keeps the Union's standard hardpoints and Castellani's hand-tuned joints on a chassis built for Protect First: a shield arm, an evacuation cradle on the back, and room in the cab for a medic. It is named after Carthage's founding queen. Strasbourg has asked for its licences back. Tunis has not replied.

nodes.t: Crewed orbital work pods
nodes.x: One-person pods with manipulator arms that built the first stations.

nodes.t: Four-armed worker frame
nodes.x: Four arms, vestigial legs used as anchors, and a big thruster pack. The standard station worker frame, and the one the workers armed in the labour dispute.

nodes.t: Long-duration salvage frame
nodes.x: A bigger worker frame with solar-fuel power for multi-day shifts and a tether harpoon for salvage. Safety yellow with hazard stripes.

nodes.t: Militarised Rigger with spike driver
nodes.x: Officially a station-security variant. In practice, a Rigger with armour plates, an RD-12 spike driver and a boarding harpoon. Every bloc has bought some.

nodes.t: First purpose-built space combat frame
nodes.x: Built for the catapults of the first warships, with no legs and a Halcyon linear rifle in place of construction tools. Nobody yet knows how it should fight. Its first instructor is writing the manual as he goes.

nodes.t: Luna's first frame built for Earth
nodes.x: The first frame the lunar foundries built for a gravity they don't have: vacuum-cast titanium-foam armour, Rigger joints rebuilt for six times the load, an ice-water fuel cell, and a sealed cockpit with its own air for smoke, gas and fallout. A rescue cradle folds out of the chest. Luna couldn't test it, so it was tested in the Atacama. The Republic gave the first twelve to the UN in 2183 as a gift, white from the foundry and armed with whatever Geneva chose to fit, and they went to the white squads' best crews. It is the Republic's overture to the UN, made in hardware.

nodes.t: A firebreak frame for a burning planet
nodes.x: A Tellus rebuilt for the fires that come every summer now: mirror-finished heat shields that throw back radiant heat, a dozer blade and trenching cutters for cutting firebreaks, and water bladders on the back that it fills from any river. From Shackleton the fire seasons show up on the Earth's face as brown smudges, and the Republic built the Albedo for them. The white squads first took it to the fire lines in Provence and Liguria in 2184, and the Union's own fire services asked to borrow two.

nodes.t: Ring power for the white squads' best
nodes.x: The Republic's prototype for the best pilots in the white squads: a Tellus rebuilt around a rectenna that draws beamed power from the Republic's own relay satellites, which it has offered to park over any UN operation. Under the relay it never runs dry; away from one it falls back on the Tellus's ice-water cell. It carries a lunar-built coil carbine, a tether harpoon and a sealed rescue capsule for four in the chest. Two have been built, and after Mong Hsat one was refitted as the Defender: heavier plate, a tall shelter shield and a heavy coil rifle, built to stand between incoming fire and an evacuation. Halcyon would give a great deal for what the Republic is giving away. Stencilled inside the cockpit hatch, in the Republic's own lettering: space is dark and cold without it.

nodes.t: Seen once, behind the Pact line at Talysh
nodes.x: Photographed in 2169 behind the Pact line at the Battle of the Talysh Mountains, recovering wrecked Tieniu cores rather than fighting. US photo interpreters noted a cockpit with no canopy and no hatch, cooling lines running into the seat, and Cyrillic stencils ground off and painted over. Its leg forgings match OKB-7's interceptor landing gear. File status: ██████████ ██ ████████.

nodes.t: The two frames left in the surf at Yonaguni
nodes.x: Two of the frames from the Yaeyama Incidents were left behind in the surf. Cast hull armour with weld seams like Tianlong's, but the welds are robot-laid, which Tianlong's plants weren't supposed to manage until 2179. Drum-fed rifles with Type-07 rifling. Radios with no maker's marks and a frequency plan nobody in the Pact admits to. Japan kept both hulls, published nothing and asked nobody. Present location of hulls: ██████ ███████ ███████.

nodes.t: The frame that carried the Raijin break-in team
nodes.x: Found abandoned in a drainage culvert two kilometres from the Tsukuyomi Lab perimeter. Halcyon-pattern wing-binder hinges with the part numbers drilled out, a Vauclair-Ehrlich sensor head, and radar-absorbent panelling nobody in Grey Lantern's catalogue offers. The captured contractor said it arrived by container and he never saw who loaded it. Halcyon's reply to Japan's inquiry was ███ █████ ███ ██████.

nodes.t: Four arms, a core drill, and nobody's survey
nodes.x: A Colony One survey drone photographed it at the bottom of Melas Chasma: a four-armed frame with Rigger shoulders, a core drill where a manipulator should be, and a sealed cargo pod with refrigeration fins on its back. Ascension's last inventory lists no frame of that description. The drone's next three passes were jammed. Contents of cargo pod: ████████.

nodes.t: A restraint frame with nothing in it
nodes.x: Swiss customs photographs of a crate bound for Marseille: a load-bearing exoframe with joint brakes and an armoured cab in the chest, the same pattern as the Field Cohort's, but built for something much larger, and empty. The consignee was a shipping agent in ████████. Halden told the ethics panel the frame was surplus. It did not say surplus to what.

nodes.t: Raid frames that move like something alive
nodes.x: Indian Army designation for the frames that came ashore at Ratnagiri in 2180 and burned the fuel depot in forty minutes. Garrison hips and a Tieniu torso welded together the way the desert workshops build Haboobs, but the limbs are sheathed in bundles of grey-red fibre that tighten and relax like muscle. Engineers who recovered a severed forearm found polymer strands soaked in a nutrient gel, and logged that it was still warm two days later. The pilots keep fighting after wounds that should stop them. The soldiers called them rakshasa, demons, and the name stuck in the files. The crews are the monsoon bands. Origin of fibre: ███████ ███████ ██ ███ ████.

nodes.t: Its wounds closed between photographs
nodes.x: Photographed twice by a League coastal patrol at Ras Hafun, a week apart, months after the Kafila ambush, beside a dhow-ferry loading for the crossing to India. In the first photograph its left thigh is torn open to the frame. In the second the wound has closed under a ridged, pinkish sheath. The muscle bundles are the Rakshasa's pattern, but these carry no gel lines. Khartoum's medical council asked to see the photographs, then asked who else had seen them. The keepers recognised the crew. Present location: ████████.

nodes.t: One frame, one voice, and no heat in the cab
nodes.x: Seen once, in 2186, after a landslide buried a hill village above Makassar. Before the provincial rescue teams arrived, a grey frame of ordinary size had dug out forty-one people and laid them in a row along the road, then walked into the forest. Its parts came from three blocs. Survivors said it paused before every choice, briefly, the way one person thinks rather than the way a crew confers. A rescue drone's thermal camera found no heat in the cab. The designation is the one stencilled on a crate at the Makassar pump works the following week. Occupant: ███████.

supers.label: Supers
supers.intro: Super robots appear in Gen 3. Each one is a different answer to the same question: what can the human spirit be made to do? Some programs harness it, some encourage it, some abuse it. Only the ███████ line comes from ███ ████████. The rest are human work: heretical science, latent spirit, or technology pushed further than it should go.
turns: Ascension's Ares mission brought back ████ ████ █████. Outside ███████ ████, almost nobody knows.
A leash made of a person
H-17, the growth Halden calls its first, only went still once a human mind bonded with it. Every Halden pilot since has been chosen to be a leash.
A year ago the United States unveiled the Concord class as a deterrent. Every hidden program in the world sped up overnight.
Thirteen ways to use a soul

Leashed, befriended, consumed, shared, disciplined, preserved, replaced, knighted, divided, hired, escaped, held in trust, hunted in packs. Five answer to no government. Each is a first draft of a philosophy that will outlive Earth, though not always the one its authors meant.

In Tangier, a workshop collective builds a giant from the North African Front's wreckage and elects its crew. When the war ends, the Commonwealth asks it to serve, and it is the only super that ever agreed to.
fams: One █████ source, treated two opposite ways.
Heretical science. The pilot becomes the control system.
Technology pushed too far, and made to work. The first super built in series, from a company Congress chartered.
Change the network, not the pilot.
Latent spirit and a fusion reactor. Nobody agrees which one is doing the work.
A knight for a union that put its giants on trial.
A country between the blocs, built in two halves.
Lunar engineering, built to the treaty every bloc vetoed.
Scrap, volunteers, and a crew that votes.
Heretical science outside any bloc. The dead, still choosing.

nodes.x: Entry withheld. Recovered by ARES-1 in 2156. ███ ███████, ██████ ███████████, neither clearly █████ nor ████. ███ ██████ ████████ ██ █████ ████████. Present location: ███████ ████. Further access by order of ███ █████████ █████████ only.

nodes.t: The first crewed Mars landing
nodes.x: Launched by Ascension from the orbital elevator about thirty years ago. Officially a geology mission whose crew came home to a parade. The mission log has a forty-hour gap, and two of the four crew never gave another interview. In 2186, one of those two led the settlers who founded Colony One.

nodes.t: Sealed orbital laboratory
nodes.x: A sealed station in high orbit, built during Gen 1 to hold ███ ████████: too dangerous to bring down to Earth, too valuable to abandon. Most Ascension staff believe Station Nine is a fuel depot.

nodes.t: Growing giant tissue from ███████ samples
nodes.x: The Halden Institute bought tissue samples ████ ███████ ████, or stole them; even Halden isn't sure which. Its Geneva laboratories spent a decade learning to grow the tissue into structure. Each culture gets an accession number; most never grow past a sample.

nodes.t: Activated six years ago
nodes.x: The first culture accession to mature to full size. Accession numbers count cultures, not giants: the sixteen before it died as samples. On activation it killed two technicians. Then it went still the moment its first pilot came online through the contact interfaces, in a test cab bolted to the laboratory rig. The restraint frame was built around it in the weeks afterwards. H-17 was lost in a League proxy war three years ago.

nodes.t: The spirit as leash
nodes.x: Two separately grown organisms in the same pattern of restraint frame: a load-bearing exoframe with joint brakes, armour panels and an armoured operator cab in the chest. Each is bonded to a pilot Halden chose for psychological profile rather than skill, and is calm only while that pilot is connected through the cab. The tissue moves itself. The bundle from the grid carries perfusion, cooling and the suppression cycle, and off the bundle a giant lasts as long as its heat and metabolite load allow: minutes in a hard fight. H-31 matures faster than H-24 and needs nearly twice the cooling. Halden treats pilots as a replaceable part of the restraint system, and has already replaced one: ████ ███████, aged ██.

nodes.t: In the tank, and it has chosen a pilot
nodes.x: Still growing in Geneva under a laboratory accession, never commissioned. At night, with the suppression cycle at full strength, its monitors record coordinated movement, which suppression is supposed to make impossible. Last month it went still for the first time, on the night a laboratory cleaner's fourteen-year-old daughter waited out a shift in the observation gallery. It is calm whenever she is in the building and restless whenever she isn't. Halden's scientists have told the ethics panel. They have not told her.

nodes.t: The spirit as partner
nodes.x: H-17, after its restraint frame shattered and its pilot died in a League proxy war. A League mechanic found it in the sand and saw what Halden never had: the suppression cycle was causing the distress Halden treated as aggression. With the cycle cut, it stopped fighting. The mechanic rebuilt the wrecked cab around a scavenged Sirocco cockpit and pilots it from inside the chest. With no grid bundle it lives on what the League brings it: water, feedstock and rest, delivered by Kafila carriers. It carries a Type-01Q cannon like a pistol. Every bloc wants it recovered or destroyed. Its pilot wants to help people.

nodes.t: Study ███ ████████ where it was found
nodes.x: Under the ethics panel's review, Halden's surviving scientists have proposed the only program the panel might approve: a sealed, supervised station in ██████ █████████, run on evidence, where nothing is grown or altered that can't be justified as necessary. The panel's conditions run to four hundred pages. They are the first draft of how the Union would govern Mars.

nodes.t: Khartoum learns to heal the Jinn
nodes.x: The people who keep the Jinn alive have learned to culture its tissue to patch its wounds, and found that the grafts adapt to whatever body they are given. Khartoum's medical council has started trials on burn victims. The keepers' rule is that the Jinn is cared for, not commanded. Not everyone in the League sees a medicine. The raid cadres who never accepted Protect First see soldiers who don't die.

nodes.t: Direct brain control of small frames
nodes.x: Before the capsule, Department Zero tested direct neural control on small frames, using volunteers who were not always volunteers. Subjects enrolled: ██. Subjects discharged: █.

nodes.t: The spirit consumed
nodes.x: The pilot is sealed in a fluid capsule and their nervous system becomes the control system. With no body to protect, the frame is built far past normal limits. A cable-fed reactor carriage follows it on tracks. Every sortie does cumulative damage to the pilot's nervous system. Officials set a nominal sortie allowance, and few pilots reach it. The name means the Deathless, because the machine outlives every pilot.

nodes.t: Designed for a pilot who never leaves
nodes.x: The second Koschei has a rear service assembly for installing the pilot and running life support, and no emergency extraction at all. Department Zero calls this an engineering simplification. Its first pilot, ██████ █. ████████, was installed in the spring. In the third week the interface began returning the same three words on every channel, in the pilot's own phrasing: let me out. Department Zero has classified it as signal noise. The engineers who wrote the interface have stopped coming to the trials.

nodes.t: Augmented, but never consumed
nodes.x: The Indian pilots augmented for the breakthrough groups refused transfer to Department Zero and wrote an oath instead. Enhancement is equipment, issued for a duty and owed back to the unit. No pilot is sealed in a capsule. The strong defend those who can't be changed. Their crews call them ashva, horses, bred and sworn for the line. Moscow hasn't decided whether it can tolerate them; Beijing pretends they don't exist.

nodes.t: Splitting neural load across two pilots
nodes.x: A US study found that two pilots on linked interfaces could run a frame far too complex for one. The test pairs also started finishing each other's sentences.

nodes.t: The spirit shared
nodes.x: A 40 m super-heavy built from scaled-up real-robot technology: the first full-scale HT-20 plant, built years before anyone could fit one in a normal frame, an electrothermal cannon, a stake driver the size of a tree. One Army pilot and one Air Force pilot share the neural load, and it only works if they trust each other completely. A dozen exist. The scarce part is compatible pilot pairs, not hardware. It was the first super the world saw, and it was built to be seen.

nodes.t: Three-pilot trials
nodes.x: A three-pilot version. In trials, the third pilot can't always tell afterwards which memories are their own.

nodes.t: A calm mind steadies the fusion loop
nodes.x: During Amaterasu trials, staff noticed the reactor ran steadier when one technician was on the console, a former shrine attendant who meditated on shift. Tsukuyomi Lab quietly began recruiting from shrines.

nodes.t: The spirit disciplined
nodes.x: The Amaterasu reactor would never fit in a normal frame, so the lab built a mech big enough for the reactor. White, blue and red, with a sun-disc chest and radiator fins that glow under load. It holds stable only with a shrine-trained pilot. Engineers call it biofeedback; priests call it the kami. Lab file ███-7 calls it ███████████ ████████. Fusion lets it fire a scaled-up BX-0 continuously, which the Raijin's capacitor-fed emitter can't do. It is the one weapon Japan legally cannot own.

nodes.t: Three trainees, one active pilot
nodes.x: Pilots are trained in a mountain shrine that also serves as a JSDF facility. Training takes years of discipline before the trainee ever touches the controls. Only one is ready.

nodes.t: Mind-maps sold to families in orbit
nodes.x: Vireo's shell companies have started selling mind-mapping off-world. The first buyers are the families crewing Tianlong's prospecting tenders, who record their elders so a house never loses what it knows. Nobody asked Beijing. The families treat the recordings as part of the house's capital, bargained over like any other asset.

nodes.t: Recording a dying person's mind
nodes.x: Vireo began as a medical startup offering terminal patients a recording of their mind. For years the recordings did nothing. Then they started running.

nodes.t: Eleven pilots, recorded before they died
nodes.x: Terminally ill and fatally wounded pilots from every bloc, recorded with consent, or something like it. They argue about whether they are the pilots or copies of them.

nodes.t: The spirit preserved
nodes.x: A giant run by the mind-maps of eleven dead pilots, built from parts Vireo bought quietly from every bloc. They vote on every action, and they have chosen to intervene where no government will: evacuations, disasters, and wars that the blocs are content to let burn. No government has discovered it yet.

nodes.t: The spirit replaced
nodes.x: Beijing's answer to the Concord and to Department Zero at once: a giant built on Tieshan engineering, with a Tianshu core in the chest and one unaugmented officer in an armoured cab who approves what the network proposes. It walks on four Salt Cores that the network runs and the officer can't touch. No compatible pairs, no shrine, no capsule: any graduate of the Order 21 course can sit in it. Tianlong has built four and has tooling for forty. It is named for the bird of the old story who set out to fill the sea one pebble at a time. The Concord is no longer the only super built in series. Nobody has yet asked what the officer is for while the link holds, or what the giant does when it doesn't.

nodes.t: The spirit escaped
nodes.x: The one Koschei pilot who reached the sortie allowance and kept going. On what was meant to be her last sortie she cut the range's command link, turned her frame north and walked it off the test ground with the reactor carriage tracking behind her. Department Zero lists the frame as destroyed in testing. Its pilot is still sealed in the capsule, her nerves failing more slowly than the medical staff predicted, and nobody knows whose side she is on, only whose side she is not. The range crews named her for the warrior princess who chained Koschei in the old tale. Delhi's officers keep her file open.

nodes.t: The spirit knighted
nodes.x: Castellani's answer to Halden, and the only super the ethics panel has approved: nothing grown, nothing implanted, nothing its pilot can't walk away from. A red-and-gold knight scaled up from the Saetta, with a capacitor-fed plasma blade the crews call Durendal, a tower shield, and a command horn, Olifant, that ties every lance within a hundred kilometres into one picture. Its pilot is the ace who flew the Saetta, and the panel's one condition is that the pilot may refuse any order. Strasbourg presents it as the heir of Roland and Charlemagne's paladins, and every member state's schoolchildren know the song. In the song, Roland dies because he is too proud to sound his horn. Castellani built the horn first.

nodes.t: The spirit divided
nodes.x: A super in two halves: the lower built in Calgary, the upper in Montreal, standing as one giant only when they lock together. Each half carries one pilot, and the pair share the neural load on an interface Boreal licensed from the Twin-Pilot Load Study, which Canada's share of the defence fund helped pay for. The two pilots have trained together for six years, one from each side of a line nobody has drawn yet. Boreal meant it as the picture of a country that holds together. When Canada splits, the halves end up on opposite sides of the Manitoba–Ontario line, and so do the pilots.

nodes.t: The spirit held in trust
nodes.x: The Republic's answer to the giants on Earth, and the only super built to a treaty: Shackleton Works designed it to the third clause of the orbital draft every bloc vetoed, so it carries no reactor and nothing it couldn't explain to Geneva. Its frame is vacuum-cast in lunar composites around Marlinspike catapult gear, with a linear core the Works designed itself, powered off the ring and the Republic's own relays. The Republic's books list it as a yard tug, which nobody believes. It carries no bloc's markings. In the war it walks through the breaches at Tranquility, and when the Republic closes the lanes to Earth it stands over the slipway in the UN's white. UNEL's Luna bastion is named for it.

nodes.t: The spirit hired
nodes.x: Grey Lantern's super, assembled from Concord parts that left Joint Heavy Systems' depots on paperwork nobody can trace: a salvaged HT-20 plant, one and a half sets of limbs, and a cab rebuilt for whoever is paying. The twin-pilot interface only works for a pair who trust each other completely, so Grey Lantern pairs strangers on contract and sedates away the difference. It has never fought the same way twice and has never been quite right. It is for hire by the week, and the container ship that carried it through the Panama Canal is why Panama now opens every container.

nodes.t: The spirit hunts in packs
nodes.x: Moscow's answer to giants it can't match in the open: six Volks rebuilt by OKB-7 as a hunting pack, with lighter armour, spiked climbing feet, tether harpoons, and Type-12 rail rifles loaded with tungsten penetrators. Their links give all six pilots one picture of the quarry. The method is old: cable the legs, bring it down, go for the cab. The pilots are augmented volunteers from the breakthrough groups, the last generation Department Zero will ever train. Their first quarry is Morevna. They have found her twice and come back without her both times, and their reports have stopped calling her a target. In the war they hunt Jingweis across Central Asia, and when the Ascendancy closes Department Zero it keeps the pack, which by then swears the Nashik Oath in Russian.

nodes.t: The spirit volunteered
nodes.x: Projected. In the shipbreaking yards at Tangier, a workshop collective of Moroccan mechanics and Southern Crossing volunteers, most of them Spanish and many of them Catalan, builds a giant from what the North African Front leaves behind. Its spine is a cut-down section of a scrapped Spanish dock ship's bottom hull, with keel and curved bilge ribs reshaped into its pelvis, lower back and shoulder structure, its limbs are wrecked Mistrals and Siroccos, and its heart is a bank of re-tuned Q-Mix turbines. Nobody owns it. The workshop is run by assembly, the crew is elected and paid the same as the welders, everyone eats at the same table, and the hull is painted red and black under slogans in Darija, Spanish and Catalan. Like the Charter's frames it is named for a wind: the Tramuntana, the north wind of Catalonia. It holds the Strait while the ferries cross. When the war ends, the Commonwealth asks it to serve rather than ordering it to, and the assembly votes yes.

conflicts.label: Conflicts
conflicts.intro: Thirty years of conflict, from the Ares mission in 2156 to the founding of Colony One, the first permanent settlement on another planet, and the fault lines that run from them into the Third World War. Each one explains something in the other trees: a doctrine, a weapon, a stolen design, or a super robot. The dashed column is projected: the war itself, which hasn't happened yet.
turns: At Iron Gate, four Garrisons destroyed a tank column in eleven minutes. Within a year every bloc had ordered mechs.
The theft that armed the East
The Pact lost the Battle of the Talysh Mountains but came away with LR-1 plans and a Mk.I core. Every Eastern linear weapon starts there.
The Zarqa Campaign introduced drop-and-strike. The Air Umbrella, the hunter-killer lance and the Harrier all exist because of it.

The Lunar Republic builds every bloc's first warships, and its domes are fighting a cold war over whether it owes the planet below anything. Each bloc is building its own way into orbit so that it never has to depend on the Moon.
At Mong Hsat the UN destroyed a warlord every bloc had armed, because none of them could veto it without saying so. It was the first time Geneva had won anything by force, and every bloc noticed.
The Concord reveal turned super robots into a public arms race, while the two supers nobody controls are out protecting civilians.
Beijing wants Department Zero shut down; Moscow and Delhi won't allow it. On a map the Pact is still one bloc. Its own staff officers no longer think so.
fams: Where the blocs fight each other by proxy, and where a pan-African bloc takes shape.
The Pact's borders, the wars along them, and the line it will break along.
Two Western blocs that are allies on paper, and the hemisphere Washington considers its own.
Japan's quiet front line, the factories everyone wants, and the islands to the south.
Where nobody has fought a real war yet.

nodes.t: Future League states refuse bloc membership
nodes.x: Resource states across the Middle East, Africa and South Asia jointly refused to join any bloc. It made them neutral on paper and a battleground in practice.

nodes.t: United States vs insurgent armour in the Zagros foothills
nodes.x: The first mech combat. Four Brannock-Hale M4 Garrisons with M30s and ATGM tubes ambushed a tank column from a ravine the tanks couldn't climb, and destroyed it in eleven minutes. Within a year every bloc had ordered mechs.

nodes.t: Iron Gate's final phase
nodes.x: The United States tried dropping licensed Sparrowhawks behind insurgent lines by tiltrotor. The mechs did well; the tiltrotors did not, and nine were shot down in a month. Halcyon's answer was a mech that could fly itself in.

nodes.t: United States vs a Pact-backed government
nodes.x: Officially the Zarqa Campaign, after the Jordanian city where it began. Kestrels made their combat debut with drop-and-strike, landing, fighting and leaving inside their battery limit. Pact advisers taught the defenders to hide for forty minutes and then hit the swap pits. Every bloc's doctrine since has been a reaction to this war.

nodes.t: Desert militias vs every bloc's supply lines
nodes.x: In the wreckage of the Zarqa Campaign, militias in Haboob frames raided convoys from all sides until foreign presence cost more than it was worth. A year later the African states founded the Pan-African League on armed neutrality, and the Gulf states, Pakistan and Bangladesh signed on as associates.

nodes.t: UN frames escort food through the raid zone
nodes.x: In the Convoy Raids the militias hit UN food convoys as readily as any bloc's. Geneva asked every bloc for escort frames and all three refused, so it bought Copperbelt mining walkers and Technical Refits, painted them white and crewed them with volunteers. When the blocs left, the white frames stayed. The new League let them use its roads on one condition: they never fired except to protect a convoy. They kept to it, and they were the only foreign frames the League let in.

nodes.t: League factions backed by the Union, the Pact and Grey Lantern
nodes.x: A League civil war that became three proxy wars at once, fought in Siroccos and Lantern Customs. The Union secretly deployed Halden's H-17 to end it. Its restraint frame failed, its pilot died, and it vanished into the dunes. A white convoy's escort filmed it falling, and Geneva sent the footage to every parliament in the Union on the same morning. Months later, a League mechanic walked out of the desert with it. The war also opened a rift that never closed: the League's Gulf associates had bankrolled the losing side.

nodes.t: An unrestrained giant protecting civilians
nodes.x: Reports keep coming from the Great Sand Sea of a giant that stands between militias and villages, then leaves. Three blocs have sent teams to recover it. None have come back with it.

nodes.t: An unidentified giant in a city under shelling
nodes.x: During a Pact-backed bombardment of Herat, an unknown giant held the Malan Bridge over the Hari River open for nine hours while civilians crossed, then disappeared. No bloc has claimed it. It was the Choir. The Pact vetoed Geneva's resolution condemning the bombardment, so the Secretary-General read the names of Herat's dead into the record instead. It took four hours.

nodes.t: The League promises to fight for something
nodes.x: The League's members, joined by Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia, signed a charter in Khartoum: mutual defence, shared reconstruction, and a promise to protect people before territory. The Gulf associates were invited and didn't come. Qadira moved its design office to Khartoum the same month, and took over the Union's licence plant in Tunis along with most of the French and Italian engineers who ran it. It is the first time the League has promised to fight for anything except being left alone.

nodes.t: Influence, not territory, from the Gulf to Bangladesh
nodes.x: Projected. The Gulf states, Iraq, Iran, Pakistan and Bangladesh become a frontline held by influence rather than territory: the League leans on the Gulf and Iraq, Beijing on Pakistan, Delhi on Bangladesh, and everyone fights over Iran.

nodes.t: From Morocco to the Nile
nodes.x: Projected. The Union's old Maghreb partners are Charter states now, and every power that needs the Mediterranean wants its southern shore. The fighting runs from Morocco to the Nile. The League fights it as the African Union, and after the war it becomes the African Commonwealth.

nodes.t: The Jinn's tissue cultures go missing
nodes.x: Raiders who had crossed the Arabian Sea to raid India's coast for twenty years, and fought for the League since the Convoy Raids, ambushed a Kafila convoy carrying the Jinn's tissue cultures to Khartoum. Two crews died and four cultures are still missing. Khartoum says it was bandits. The keepers know the raiders' names, because until the Charter they were on the same side.

nodes.t: A recovery team goes into the Great Sand Sea
nodes.x: One of the three teams sent to recover the Jinn. The aircraft were American; the frames were Lantern Customs with their serials ground off; the recovery rig was built to carry something very large that was still alive. Two frames came back. The after-action report runs to six pages, five of them blacked out. The surviving page ends: ███ ██████ ███ ███ ████ ██ ████ ██ ███ ████ ██ ███ █████.

nodes.t: Healing made into a weapon, then a duty
nodes.x: Projected. The missing cultures reappear on the North African Front, inside raid battalions whose soldiers survive wounds that should kill them. As the war grinds on, the League stops arguing: grafting is how it keeps anyone alive on the worst fronts, and then simply how it keeps people. The raid cadres who brought the cultures commit the front's worst raids, and the most changed of the grafted follow them. When the Commonwealth finally catches them, they are sent furthest of all, to Jupiter. Umoja begins there, still using the keepers' word for it: care.

nodes.t: Europeans and Americans go south to the Charter
nodes.x: Projected. As the European Front breaks and American cities are mobilised for the war economy, people who want no part of either bloc go south: across the Mediterranean to Tunis, Algiers and Alexandria, and across the Atlantic to Dakar and Lagos. Many are French and Italian, with family ties to the old Maghreb partnership; many more are leftists with no room left in either bloc's politics. They bring languages, engineers and arguments, and the Commonwealth that comes out of the war is more plural for it.

nodes.t: Pact vs US-backed Afghan forces in the Wakhan Corridor
nodes.x: The Tieniu's combat debut. Crews fired standing, outside the cannon's safe envelope, and the recoil threw frames off their feet; by the second week they were kneeling to fire, as the manual said. The Pact also captured a dozen M30s, which became the Type-07.

nodes.t: Pact vs United States, over Azerbaijan
nodes.x: A Pact push into Azerbaijan brought the United States in. At the Battle of the Talysh Mountains, a handful of Merlins with LR-1 linear rifles destroyed a Tieniu column from above. OKB-7's new Korsaks were dropped to hold the passes ahead of the column, and the drop scattered across the mountains. The Pact lost the battle but won the intelligence war: within a year it had LR-1 plans and a captured Mk.I capacitor core.

nodes.t: Pact digs in; a US probe is repulsed
nodes.x: After the Caspian Crisis the Pact dug Tieshan firing lines into its borders. A US probing raid, Operation Highland, ran into one and lost a third of its frames in an afternoon. No bloc has tried to invade the Pact since.

nodes.t: Pact-backed offensive into western Afghanistan
nodes.x: The debut of OKB-7's breakthrough groups: Medveds and Mamonts opening gaps for Tieshan waves. Observers also saw a fast, wolf-like frame that moved in ways no ordinary pilot could survive. It was the first sighting of the Volk.

nodes.t: Moscow stockpiles siege weapons
nodes.x: Kalibr-305 mortars, Iskra cannons and MTU-7 trucks are gathering near the border. Satellite photos show a 50 m shape lying across several oversize flatcars under tarpaulins. Every bloc is asking what war Moscow is preparing for. Some of the people asking work in Beijing.

nodes.t: India joins the Pact as a junior partner
nodes.x: India backed the Hari River Offensive with airfields and fuel, and a year later joined the Pact outright. The price was industrial: OKB-7 opened a second Medved and Mamont line at Nashik, and Indian officers joined the breakthrough groups and took the augmentation that came with them: after twenty years of raiders who wouldn't die, Delhi wanted pilots who could catch them, and accepted Moscow's way of making them, however little it liked it. Beijing welcomed a third member. Delhi has voted with Moscow ever since.

nodes.t: Beijing's planning network names the second front
nodes.x: Asked to plan for a two-front war, Tianshu returned a plan in which the second front was Moscow. Beijing classified it within the hour. Within the month, someone in Moscow had read it. Beijing's position is that the network models every contingency. Moscow's is that Beijing kept asking.

nodes.t: Fourteen dead at a test range that is on no map
nodes.x: Pact state radio reported an industrial accident at a fuel depot in ██████ ██████, with fourteen dead. Satellite photographs show a test range, a reactor carriage on its side, and a frame-sized trench running north for nine kilometres before it stops. The casualty list was withdrawn after a day. Department Zero's internal number for the event is ██-183.

nodes.t: Beijing and Moscow split over Department Zero
nodes.x: At a closed session of the Pact General Staff in Astana, Beijing's delegation demanded that Department Zero be shut down and its pilot records handed over. Moscow refused, Delhi backed Moscow, and the session ended without a communiqué. Since then the Fortress Belt and the Air Umbrella have answered to Tianshu, and the breakthrough groups to Moscow. On paper there is still one General Staff.

nodes.t: UN white squads destroy a warlord's army in the Shan Hills
nodes.x: In 2174 a company of the export Tieshans guarding the Pact's Mekong dam went unpaid for a winter and walked into the Shan Hills with their frames. Their commander styled himself the Iron Sawbwa, after the old Shan princes. For ten years he ran jade mines and drug labs on forced labour, kept his Tieshans running on parts bought from both ends of the Pact, and shelled refugee camps across the Thai border for sheltering his deserters. After the Tianshu Forecast, Beijing would not let Delhi's forces near its border and Moscow would not let Beijing's in. When the Secretary-General put a resolution to the Security Council, the Pact could not veto it without explaining who had been selling him parts, and the United States would not defend a man flying Pact frames. It passed with every bloc abstaining. Two white squads went up the valley at Mong Hsat behind a Brazilian major in a Haubert. In two days they destroyed eleven Tieshans, and the Sawbwa died in the last of them. It was the first time UN frames had fired first. Geneva says it will be the last. Nobody who flew at Mong Hsat believes it.

nodes.t: The Pact breaks into Chinese and Russian–Indian blocs
nodes.x: Projected. The two General Staffs stop pretending. Central Asia, where both sides' railways meet, becomes the front. Mongolia and the Steppe outriders side with Beijing, and the fighting goes where they know the rail lines and Moscow's planners don't. The Tian Shan Rail, the Pact's only road to orbit that doesn't go through the Moon, sits on the front line, and neither side gets much use of it after the first year. What comes out of it is China and the Eurasian Ascendancy.

nodes.t: Moscow's siege trains turn west
nodes.x: Projected. Moscow's breakthrough groups and siege trains turn west into a Continental Union whose council is still voting on how to respond. Twenty-six national contingents wait on twenty-six parliaments while the line gives way from the Baltic to the Black Sea. Behind the line, a few cities split along the old Maghreb question, street by street. What survives is refounded as the Transatlantic Union. Its institutions bind tightly enough that no single member can stop the whole from acting, and a doctrine of deliberate mixing means no city splits that way again. It is still slow, but never again paralysed.

nodes.t: Washington hands frame procurement to its makers
nodes.x: A year after Iron Gate, Congress needed mechs faster than the Pentagon could buy them. The Defense Production Partnership Act let Brannock-Hale and Halcyon design, build, crew-train and maintain their own frames, with company engineers holding reserve commissions and company depots counted as Army bases. It was meant to last until the first production run was delivered. It is still in force, and the two companies' lobbyists wrote most of its renewals.

nodes.t: United States vs Continental Union, undeclared
nodes.x: A trade dispute over North African partners turned into two weeks of undeclared strikes. US aircraft destroyed Union hydrogen depots and grounded the Écuyer fleet without firing on a single mech. The Union never forgot, and rebuilt its doctrine around never being blind or stranded again. The Union's North African partners drew their own lesson: Strasbourg could not protect them.

nodes.t: United States vs Union over Arctic seabed claims
nodes.x: The first hunter-killer lance action. Pavises jammed a Kestrel flight's landing approach, then shot four of them as they transformed, and a red Castellani Falco finished the rest. Within a year the United States had refitted its front-line Kestrels as Harriers, a heavier design first drawn up against the Pact's rockets. The Union got its first famous ace. Norway, a US ally, watched two allies fight over its own archipelago and began asking which of them would defend it.

nodes.t: The United States unveils its super robots
nodes.x: The United States publicly revealed the Concord class as a deterrent. Every other bloc's hidden program sped up overnight, and every intelligence service started asking who else has one.

nodes.t: Canada asks for observer status in the Union
nodes.x: After the Concord reveal, Canada's parliament learned that its share of the joint North American defence fund had paid for HT-20 plants it was never told about, built by companies that answer to Washington before Ottawa. A motion to seek observer status in the Union passed by eleven votes. Washington called it a procedural matter. Strasbourg sent a delegation the same week.

nodes.t: Canada splits along the Manitoba–Ontario line
nodes.x: Projected. The Halifax Motion's eleven votes become a partition. The western provinces stay with the United States; Ontario, Quebec and the Atlantic provinces join the Union, and the United Kingdom, Iceland and Norway, after thirty years of paying Washington's levy, follow. Quebec's hydrogen fields come with them, and the Union's fuel cells are never short of hydrogen again. The line between the two Canadas is fought over for the rest of the war.

nodes.t: Mexico joins; Central America and the canal are taken
nodes.x: Projected. Mexico joins the United States, and the canal where Panama once searched every ship is taken with the rest of Central America. It keeps the hemisphere's trade in Washington's hands, and by the war's end the country calls itself the United States of the Americas.

nodes.t: Brazil reaches for Africa and is cut off
nodes.x: Projected. Brazil, flying European frames and trading with Africa, tries to align with the African Union. The Isthmus Seizure cuts the hemisphere in two, US forces push down the Andes and into the Amazon, and the continent becomes a front instead of an ally.

nodes.t: Refugees flee to the ice
nodes.x: Projected. Refugees from the Canadian Front go north into the Arctic archipelago and Greenland; refugees from the South American Front go south, to Tierra del Fuego and the Antarctic stations. Nobody fights over the ice, which is the point. The communities that survive there learn to live on almost no heat, almost no power and almost no outside help, and stop trusting anyone from the warm places. A few say a giant walked with them across the ice and never said a word. They will carry all of it a very long way.

nodes.t: Places the war is not allowed to enter
nodes.x: Projected. The UN cannot stop the war, so it names the places the war may not enter: Geneva, the hospital ships, the refugee camps on the Falklands, the Antarctic stations, and the roads of the Polar Exodus and the Southern Crossing. Most of the time the fronts go round them, because every side needs somewhere to exchange prisoners, and the white squads are the only people all of them let into the ruins. When a front doesn't go round, the white squads fight whoever it belongs to. At Punta Arenas they hold the harbour for a week against a raiding column sent for the Antarctic stations' fuel, until it turns back. After Vancouver, the UN's casualty count reaches the lunar yards before any bloc's version does.

nodes.t: The Union's council can't agree how to answer Khartoum
nodes.x: When Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia signed the Khartoum Charter, the Union's council needed every member to agree on a response. It met eleven times in four months, could not agree on sanctions, aid or even a statement, and finally issued a communiqué regretting the partners' decision. The Union still has no army of its own: its lances are national contingents, each needing its own parliament's vote to deploy. Strasbourg calls this consensus. Its former partners call it absence. In Marseille, Lyon and Turin, families from the Maghreb who have been Union residents for three generations are starting to be asked which side they are on.

nodes.t: The Secretary-General names the coming war
nodes.x: Months after Mong Hsat, Secretary-General Joaquim Esteves went before the General Assembly with a list: siege trains on the Pact's borders, Concords on parade, a Pact General Staff that no longer meets, a Union council that can't decide anything, Panama opening every container, and warships on the Moon. Every bloc, he said, is preparing for a war it expects someone else to start. He asked for one thing: a standing UN frame force, paid for by every member and answerable to the Assembly. The Assembly voted for it 141 to 9. The Council vetoed its funding three times, once for each bloc. Esteves now asks members for frames one at a time, and more of them are saying yes.

nodes.t: JSDF vs unidentified frames
nodes.x: Unmarked frames landed on Yonaguni and Hateruma, two of Japan's outlying Yaeyama Islands. Hayates came ashore through the surf and drove them off in the JSDF's first mech combat. The attackers were never identified. Japan made no accusations and kept selling capacitors to everyone.

nodes.t: Attempted theft of the PT-X Raijin
nodes.x: An infiltration team got inside the Tsukuyomi Lab perimeter before it was stopped. The only one captured was a Grey Lantern contractor who didn't know who had hired them. The Raijin was moved, and Takemikazuchi was hidden deeper.

nodes.t: A freighter, a sealed hold, and divers who signed for life
nodes.x: A freighter under a flag of convenience sank in calm weather in the Makassar Strait. JSDF divers were first on the wreck. They found a sealed hold lined with server racks and eleven empty ████████ ████████, and their dive logs were collected by a Japanese ministry the same afternoon. Nobody in the ministry knew what they were looking at. The freighter's owner was dissolved the following week; its registered agent was a pump wholesaler in Makassar.
