ORBIT.wO9: Earth orbit and the lanes to the Moon
ORBIT.wO11: Geneva, and a crew mess on the Moon
ORBIT.wO14: The Moon, the Assembly at Shackleton
ORBIT.wO16: Tian Shan, Malapert Mountain and the L1 point
ORBIT.wO23: Juno, in the Belt, and a ministry in Beijing
ORBIT.wO24: The Belt, and the lanes home to China
ORBIT.wO25: Mars, and the panel's bunker under Strasbourg

ERA_NOTE: Three blocs and a neutral Japan

Before mechs. The United States, the Continental Union and the Eurasian Pact already face each other, and Japan stays out. Resource states across the Middle East, Africa and South Asia sign the Non-Aligned Declaration in 2159, three years after the Ares crew comes home from Mars. All of them share a biosphere already badly damaged by two centuries of warming, drowned coasts and failing harvests, and none of them is doing much about it. The United Nations, which moved to Geneva when New York's flood barriers failed, keeps count, and three bloc vetoes stop it doing anything else.
Mechs go to war in other people's countries

Iron Gate in the Zagros, the Pamir clash in the Wakhan Corridor, the Caspian Crisis over Azerbaijan, and an undeclared US–Union war over the Union's North African partners. Raiders from the Horn cross the Arabian Sea to a coast India can't defend. In orbit, station workers arm their Lifters.
The forty-minute war and the League

The Zarqa Campaign sets every bloc's doctrine. Convoy raids drive the blocs out of Africa and Arabia, leaving only the UN's white-painted escort frames, and in 2177 the African states found the Pan-African League on armed neutrality. The Pact digs in behind its fortress belt, and Japan fights its first mech action in the Yaeyama Islands.
Allies on paper, proxies in the sand

The two Western blocs fight at Svalbard. The Pact pushes into western Afghanistan, and India joins it. The League's civil war becomes three proxy wars in the Great Sand Sea, where Halden's H-17 is lost. In orbit, the first combat deaths, and on the Moon, Ascension's lunar half and the cities around its yard declare a republic, and the blocs carve up what is left of Ascension.
Deterrence by giants, and a home on Mars

Colony One is founded on Mars: the first permanent settlement on another planet. Above Earth, every bloc's first warships come off the Lunar Republic's slipway while each bloc builds its own way up, and the Republic's domes slide into a cold war over what Luna owes the planet below. On Earth, the Concord reveal sets off a public arms race and Moscow stockpiles siege weapons. In the Shan Hills, UN frames destroy a warlord nobody else was allowed to touch, and in Geneva the Secretary-General asks for a standing force and is vetoed three times. Meanwhile two supers that answer to no government protect civilians in the Great Sand Sea and at Herat. Underneath, the Pact splits in two behind a General Staff that now exists only on paper, Canada looks toward the Union, Mexico signs on with Washington, the League signs a defence charter in Khartoum while the Union's council deadlocks over it, and Mitsurugi starts copying its archives abroad.

The Third World War, which this atlas leads up to but doesn't tell. Its major fronts run through Canada, South America, Europe, Central Asia, North Africa, the Middle East, Oceania and Alaska, and for the first time through orbit. The UN can't stop it, but holds open cities and refugee roads through it, and it ends when Luna's fleets force the peace under the UN's flag. The map shows where the fronts are expected to run, and the five Earth powers that come out of it. Hatched states are front lines; pale fills mark influence without control.

POWERS.id: A corporate-backed hard power: materially capable, commercially aggressive, and willing to use military and economic leverage to keep Earth's authority in space.
POWERS.seed: Halcyon, Brannock-Hale and Joint Heavy Systems have worked as arms of the state since the Partnership Act. Its biological purism begins with Unaltered Crews, the Monterrey Accords bring in Mexico, and the Panama inspections hand it a reason to take Central America. Once Mexico joins, it calls itself the United States of the Americas. Its North Atlantic allies pay for its protection under the Burden Share for thirty years, are billed for every favour, and leave in the war.

POWERS.home: Strasbourg · Europe and the North Atlantic
POWERS.id: A post-national, multicultural union that places legitimacy in negotiated institutions, shared standards, and integration that can outlast the nation-state.
POWERS.seed: The Continental Union, whose council could never agree in time, refounded so that it can. The Long Session teaches it that lesson. Its oversight panels begin with Ethics Review, Eastern Canada's turn toward Europe with the Halifax Motion, and Britain's with the slipway Washington wouldn't give it.

POWERS.faith: Confucian order and AI-guided moral doctrine
POWERS.id: An optimised techno-state that treats coordination, technical competence and long-term planning as the foundations of survival. Its purity is biological: implants, network links and machine judgement are welcome, and rewriting the human body is not.
POWERS.seed: Tianlong's mass production, and Tianshu, the network that already plans its wars and by 2186 runs Tianlong's salt reactors too, because no human is trusted to. The split begins with the Tianshu Forecast and the Sealed Session, and Japan's absorption with the Osaka dispute. Its Steppe crews descend from the Mongolian outriders who scout Tianshu's frame trains.

POWERS.faith: Orthodox and Hindu traditions, no single creed
POWERS.id: A ruthlessly pragmatic power that puts its people first. Russia remembers late-21st-century wars that spent a generation of young men; India remembers letting China eclipse it. The Ascendancy will cross a line when its people's survival demands it and carry the stain afterwards, but it doesn't go looking for lines to cross.
POWERS.seed: OKB-7's heavy frames, the breakthrough groups and the augmented pilots, built in Russia and, since the Delhi Accession, in India. India comes to it already squeezed: raided for twenty years by the first enhanced soldiers and kept on Tianshu's spare-parts schedule, it distrusts both kinds of enhancement and relies on both to catch up. Department Zero, which spends pilots the way the old wars spent men, is everything the Ascendancy is founded against; the Nashik Oath, which protects them, is what it keeps. Its wolves, the Staya, are the last augmented pilots Moscow trained, and swear the Oath in Russian. Its proudest export is the people it would not keep: the Nashik pilots, sent away with its blessing to become the Ashva Compact.

POWERS.faith: Plural and culturally powerful; no faith rules
POWERS.id: A preservation-first commonwealth that values restraint, resilience and the protection of viable communities above prestige-driven expansion.
POWERS.seed: The Pan-African League and the Maghreb, bound by the Khartoum Charter and called the African Union during the war. The Harmattan is its first frame, and Protect First its first doctrine. The Tunis Works bring French and Italian engineering into its frames, and the war's Southern Crossing makes it more plural still. Its first giant, the Tramuntana, is built from scrap in Tangier by Moroccan mechanics and Spanish volunteers, and serves because it was asked. Its first act as a confident state is to catch the raid cadres it once rode beside, and put them off the planet.

HEIRS: Mexico joins and Western Canada stays. Eastern Canada, the United Kingdom, Iceland and Norway, billed for thirty years under the Burden Share, go over to the Union. Central America is taken in the war.
Too divided to act when the war comes, and refounded around institutions that can, with Eastern Canada and the North Atlantic. Its Maghreb partners go south.
Takes in India, then splits: Beijing on one side, Moscow and Delhi on the other. Central Asia is the front.
Falls into China's sphere. Part of Mitsurugi escapes to Russia and the United States.
Becomes the African Union in the war and the Commonwealth after it. Its Gulf, Pakistani and Bangladeshi associates become a contested frontline.
United Nations of Earth and Luna

Ascension's lunar half, grown into the most advanced manufacturer off Earth. Builds every bloc's first warships and gives its best frames to the UN, hardens through a cold war in its own domes, and ends the war by putting its fleets under the UN, becoming UNEL's lunar half.
United Nations of Earth and Luna
Vetoed for fifty years, ignored through the war, and handed a navy at the end of it. Its relief agencies and white squads become UNEL's two halves.

UNEL.n: United Nations of Earth and Luna
UNEL.home: Geneva and the Luna Custodian Bastion
UNEL.id: Humanity's last great central institution: a preservation-first authority over Earth and Luna, with its own navy, a planned reconstruction and a mandate to protect humanity from itself.
UNEL.seed: The Lunar Republic: Ascension's lunar half, grown into the most advanced manufacturer humanity has, building every bloc's first warships, arming the UN's white squads for nothing and fighting a cold war in its own domes over what it owes the planet below. When the war turns atomic, the Republic gives its fleets to the United Nations, which has spent fifty years being vetoed and the war holding open cities with borrowed white frames. Together they force the peace.

SPACE.home: The First City, now the US-held Colony One Bastion · dispersed
SPACE.faith: A civic religion of Martian survival
SPACE.id: The surviving remnant of the first colonial project: founded by the United States, crushed by it, and now a fleet, a network and a memory.
SPACE.seed: It is founded in 2186, on the eve of the war, as the first permanent settlement on another planet, and grows up in the war's wreckage. It starts in the gap between Washington's purity laws and what Mars does to a human body: its settlers are the people the United States had to let go in order to send anyone at all, led by one of the two Ares crew who never gave another interview. Its first roster recruited people who had already learned to go without.

SPACE.faith: Free, with a Catholic plurality and a civic faith in the charter
SPACE.id: The lawful, commercial, American-aligned Martian state, built from the wreckage of the First Martian Crisis to keep American influence on Mars without letting another colony drag Washington into war. It holds a third of Mars beside the US-held Bastion.
SPACE.seed: Two arguments from 2186 that Washington ignored. The Loyal Minority, liberals who fought Unaltered Crews from inside the government, wrote a charter for American Mars that protected every settler and kept war in Washington's hands. The river judges, Mexican water engineers on Colony One's resupply roster, brought water kept by law to a colony that only knew rationing. When Colony One breaks with Washington, the river families keep the Freehold Basin's water running for both sides and refuse to join the revolt. Afterwards the shelved charter is taken down and ratified at New Philadelphia, with the clause its loyal authors wrote in: no Martian war without Washington. It takes its idea of a giant from the Concord, which only works when two crews trust each other completely, and its first frame pilot from the river roster. It is why the Constitutionalists exist, and why they can't fight alone.

SPACE.id: An engineered, rationalist Martian state that places scientific reason and deliberate social design above inherited custom. It holds two thirds of Mars.
SPACE.seed: Halden's disgrace and the Union's answer to it: enhancement only by demonstrated necessity, and every program before a panel. The Mars Proposal is the first draft of how the Union would govern Mars, and Roland's pilot, who flies on the panel's condition that she may refuse any order, is the first person it governs that way. In the war, the Mars station refuses Strasbourg's order to grow soldiers for the front, and the panel backs it against the council. With Europe burning, the ethics panel turns its conditions toward everything beyond the Moon, and that becomes the Directorate's charter.

SPACE.id: A nomadic, hyper-capitalist Belt power organised through markets, contracts, mobile assets and exchange rather than territory, with China as its patron.
SPACE.seed: Tianlong's family-crewed prospecting tenders, out where Tianshu's plans arrive late, keeping their own ledgers and buying continuity contracts for their elders. Beijing charters them at Juno and gives them their name, and in the war it leases them its Belt ships rather than lose the Belt. In the war, the Steppe wind riders who won't take Beijing's protection ride the last launches up the Tian Shan Rail to join them.

SPACE.id: A kin-first biotechnological civilisation that offers belonging, food security and adaptation, through care that is paternalistic and strongly pro-enhancement.
SPACE.seed: A tragedy in four steps: raid bands dosed with pirated spacer therapies who cross the Arabian Sea to India, the keepers' healing tissue that their heirs steal, a war that makes grafting the price of staying alive, and a Commonwealth that finally catches them and puts them off the planet. Umoja keeps the keepers' word for it, care, but loses their rule that care is never a command.

SPACE.id: An honour-bound outer-system compact that combines mercantile independence, advanced human adaptation, strong institutions and a preservationist social order.
SPACE.seed: The Nashik Oath: augmentation as equipment owed to the unit, never consumption. In the war, the Mitsurugi engineers who leave Japan through Vladivostok bring the actuators. When the war ends, Moscow and Delhi send them away with a blessing, because the century ahead will need monster hunters who can't be made into monsters.

SPACE.faith: Theocratic: a faith of the distant sun
SPACE.id: A distant outer-system civilisation in which faith and collective identity have become central political facts.
SPACE.seed: No Earth power, and no government's super program. Its people are refugees from the Canadian and South American fronts who flee to the Arctic and the Antarctic, learn to live on almost no heat and almost no help, taught first by Arctic soldiers who could wait out a winter on a trickle of power, and carry that into the dark. The faith comes later, far out in the cold: a worship of the sun by people who can barely see it. It comes back to the inner system aboard a drifting ship that a Syndicate caravan picks up, and the Syndicate, seeing a market, encourages it.

TIMELINE.arc: An alliance leader that ends the period trusting its corporations more than its allies.
end: United States of the Americas

A corporate-backed hard power holding Mexico, Central America and Western Canada. It funds Colony One, crushes its rebellion, builds the Constitutionalists to replace it, and keeps the ruined First City as a US-held bastion.
ev: The richest bloc: armour holds, air power strikes deep.
Outbids the Union for South American lithium; Halcyon bets on batteries.
Iron Gate: four Garrisons win the first mech battle.
The Partnership Act hands frame procurement to Brannock-Hale and Halcyon.
The Caspian Crisis: Merlins win at Talysh, but the LR-1 plans are stolen.
Undeclared strikes ground the Union's fleet at its Maghreb depots.
Operation Highland breaks on the Fortress Belt.
Svalbard: a Union lance shoots Kestrels mid-transformation.
Harriers with point-defence lasers answer Svalbard and the Air Umbrella.
The Concord reveal starts a public super-robot arms race.
Unaltered Crews: biological purity becomes regulation.
Canada's Halifax Motion; Mexico signs the Monterrey Accords.
Mexico joins and Central America is taken: the United States of the Americas.
Canada splits; the west stays. South America becomes a front.
Oceania, then Alaska, and an atomic exchange that destroys Vancouver.
The Burden Share Compact: allies pay for America's carriers in hydrogen, seabed rights and shipyards.
Britain's leased Sparrowhawks are recalled for the Tiltrotor Drops and come back worn out, with an invoice.
A Kestrel swap pit goes in at Keflavik, and Iceland is told afterwards.
Halcyon threatens Britain's Kestrel support over a Haubert licence.
Norway is billed for the Harrier refit after Svalbard.
The Rio Bravo compact: water for Mexico, a parts plant for Brannock-Hale.
Britain is refused a berth at Hampton Roads and asks Strasbourg instead.
The Loyal Minority: forty-one votes against Unaltered Crews, and a charter for Mars that Washington shelves.

TIMELINE.arc: Quality, ethics, and a council that can never agree in time.
end: Transatlantic Union

Refounded in Strasbourg with Eastern Canada and the North Atlantic, around institutions no single member can stall. Its Mars program becomes the Martian Research Directorate, which keeps the Union's conditions and not its orders.
ev: Licenses the Garrison as the Écuyer.
The Maghreb Depot Strikes: blinded and grounded in two weeks.
Directive 5: blind the enemy first, then fight.
Funds Halden's ███████ tissue program in Geneva.
Opens a Haubert line in Tunis for its North African partners.
Svalbard: the hunter-killer lance and the Union's first famous ace.
Secretly sends Halden's H-17 into the Great Sand Sea, and loses it.
Directive 10: every program goes before an ethics panel.
The Long Session: the council can't agree how to answer Khartoum.
Halden proposes a supervised research station on Mars.
Roland: the only super the ethics panel approves.
The European Front: the council is still voting as the line breaks.
Eastern Canada, the United Kingdom, Iceland and Norway come over.
The Battle of Yernon: one British dreadnought breaks the Russian inner fleet.
The Admiralty asks about the Malapert docks; the council agrees in nine days.
The ethics panel looks up: its Mars conditions become a charter for everything beyond the Moon.
The Strasbourg Requisition: the Mars station refuses the council, and the panel backs Mars.

TIMELINE.arc: A loyal ally billed for its loyalty, until it splits down the middle and freezes.
end: Split, and sent north

The west stays with the United States and the east goes to the Transatlantic Union. The Winter War empties the towns along the line, and the camps its refugees build on the Arctic ice send people into the deep system.
ev: Snow tractors and ice-road haulers for the Arctic mines.
The Burden Share: Quebec's hydrogen goes south at Washington's price.
Boreal builds licensed Garrisons as the Tundra. Washington sets the terms; Ottawa pays them.
Washington won't export its newest sensor head, so the Caribou carries the Union's.
Montreal sells Quebec hydrogen to the Union at three times Washington's price.
After Svalbard, the Wolverine is built to be seen last.
The Aurora's pilots, one from Calgary and one from Montreal, start training together.
The Halifax Motion passes by eleven votes.
The Polaris is unveiled the same week, and both capitals claim it.
The Kenora depots: both sides start stocking a line nobody has drawn.
The Canadian Front splits the country at the Manitoba–Ontario line.
The Winter War: Canadians against Canadians, supplied from both sides.
The Northern Lift carries a million people onto the ice.

TIMELINE.arc: Mass production, then a network that plans the wars.
end: China

An AI-guided techno-state that keeps Japan in its sphere. Its charter turns the Belt's prospecting houses into the Celestial Prosperity Syndicate: a client that flies China's old hulls and keeps its own books.
ev: Tianlong's excavators, tractors and diesel factories.
The Pamir Border Clash: the Tieniu learns to kneel.
Tianshu begins as the scheduler for the frame trains.
The Fortress Belt: dug-in Tieshans that no bloc has broken.
Export Tieshans guard a Pact-funded dam on the Mekong.
Tieshan-Kai land on a Spratly reef that Tianshu chose.
The Air Umbrella, cued by Tianshu.
Mongolian outriders scout the frame trains across the steppe.
The Tianshu Forecast names Moscow as the second front.
The Sealed Session: Beijing demands Department Zero be shut down.
Order 21 and the Tianyan: the network proposes, the officer approves.
Squeezes Mitsurugi in the Osaka Licensing Dispute.
Tianlong's prospecting families start keeping their own ledgers.
The Jingwei: a super that needs no special pilot.
Darkhan's rail workshops build the KH-2 Takhi for the Steppe outriders.
Berlin's splinter collective joins Khiimori. The KH-X Tsagaan Salkhi flies.
The Pact Civil War, fought across Central Asia.
Japan falls into China's sphere; landings spread through Oceania.
The Darkhan kurultai: the Steppe splits between Beijing's protection and the Belt.
The Juno Concession: Beijing charters the Belt houses as the Celestial Prosperity Syndicate.
The Patron's Lease: Beijing's Belt ships pass to the Syndicate for the duration.

TIMELINE.arc: Quality, augmentation and siege trains, and a partner that joins because it is tired of losing.
end: Eurasian Ascendancy

Russia and India, determined that their people will never again be spent. Department Zero is closed and the Nashik Oath kept. The Nashik pilots and Mitsurugi's exiles are sent off with its blessing, and become the Ashva Compact.
ev: OKB-7 builds interceptors and bombers for deep-battle doctrine.
Turkey closes the Bosporus to frames; the Pact starts building ground-effect craft on the Caspian.
The Caspian Crisis: loses at Talysh, but steals the LR-1.
The Medved: the Pact's first frame built for quality over numbers.
The Hari River Offensive; the augmented Volk is first seen.
The Delhi Accession: India joins, and OKB-7 opens a line at Nashik.
Koschei: the pilot becomes the control system.
The Siege Question: Tsars and a 50 m shape on the flatcars.
Refuses Beijing at the Sealed Session; Delhi backs Moscow.
The Nashik Oath: augmented, but never consumed.
Morevna: a Koschei pilot walks off the range.
The Staya: six Volks sent to bring Morevna back.
The Pact Civil War, then the siege trains turn west into Europe.
Across the Bering Strait into Alaska.
Monsoon raiders cross the Arabian Sea; India has no frames to meet them.
The Ladakh withdrawal: a kneeling Tieniu on a ridge India claimed.
Delhi buys export Tieshans from Beijing, and waits on Tianshu for spares.
Kandla burns while India's Tieshans wait for parts.
Raid frames that move like something alive hit the Konkan coast.
After the Sealed Session, Tianshu stops scheduling India's spares.
At Vladivostok the Nashik pilots are given the Ark and a blessing, and sent away.

TIMELINE.arc: Neutral because everyone needs its parts, until someone wants the factory.
end: China's sphere
Japan is absorbed. The Mitsurugi engineers who left through Vladivostok carry their actuators toward the Ashva Compact.
ev: Defensive by law, and rich from exports.
After the Malacca seizures, pays for a coast guard instead of fighting.
The Japanese public meets mechs as rescuers: the Kizuna.
The Yaeyama Incidents: Hayates' first combat, against frames nobody claims.
Licence Diplomacy: sell critical parts to everyone.
Kizuna frames dig out Aceh under a rebel truce.
An infiltration team goes for the Raijin; the one captured is Grey Lantern.
Takemikazuchi: a fusion reactor that only a shrine-trained pilot can steady.
The Osaka dispute; Mitsurugi registers subsidiaries in Vladivostok and Ohio.
Someone takes the factory, and Japan falls into China's sphere.
Grain credits from Beijing, and Tianshu starts scheduling Japan's ports.
The Kansai Coalition wins the Diet on a promise to settle with Beijing.

TIMELINE.arc: From refusing every bloc to promising to protect people, and the war that breaks that promise.
end: African Commonwealth

Preservation-first and hard-won, after fighting the war as the African Union. At the war's end it catches the raid cadres it once rode beside, and puts them and the grafted who follow them off the planet. They become Umoja.
ev: Resource states sign the Non-Aligned Declaration.
Surplus Garrisons and Tieniu rebuilt as technical refits.
Mining companies armour walkers against Copperbelt raiders.
The Convoy Raids drive every bloc out.
The League is founded on armed neutrality, with Gulf associates.
Brazil seats a League delegation at the Gran Chaco ceasefire.
The Great Sand Sea War; a League mechanic finds the Jinn.
The Khartoum Charter: the Maghreb joins, and Protect First becomes doctrine.
The Harmattan: Khartoum's first designed frame.
The keepers heal the Jinn; old raiders steal its tissue.
The Tunis Works and their French and Italian engineers join the Charter.
The North African Front: the League becomes the African Union.
The grafted battalions: healing becomes a duty.
The Southern Crossing: Europeans and Americans go south.
Tangier's collective builds the Tramuntana from scrap.
Raid bands from the Horn start crossing to India on the monsoon.
At Ras Hafun, a frame whose wounds close between photographs.
The Hafun Reckoning: the raid cadres are put off the planet.

TIMELINE.arc: From a geology mission to the first permanent human home on another planet.
end: Colony One and a divided Mars

Colony One grows up in the war's wreckage, rebels against Washington, is crushed, and survives as a dispersed fleet and network, while Mars is divided along the Red Line: two thirds to the Martian Research Directorate, one third to the United States and the Constitutionalists. The First City becomes the Colony One Bastion, held directly by the United States.
ev: Station Nine is built. Officially, it is a fuel depot.
The Rivet Strike: station workers arm their Lifters.
Riggers take salvage crews out for weeks at a time.
Station Nine goes dark for nine hours.
The Tether Incident: the first combat deaths in orbit.
The first warships, with no doctrine to use them.
Every bloc builds its own way up: the Tian Shan Rail, Malapert's docks, Hampton Roads.
Colony One is founded: the first permanent settlement on another planet.
Months later, a secret landing at ███ ████ ████ in Valles Marineris.
The Orbital Front: the first war between ships.
The Lunar Mandate: the Republic's fleets end the war.
The Red Roster: Colony One recruits people who can go without.
Berth lotteries at the elevators as the harvests fail.
The Long Lift: every front sends people up.
The river judges: Mexican water engineers sign on for Colony One's first resupply.
Ascension is broken up: the Republic takes the ring and the stations, the blocs the elevators, Washington the Mars mission.
The Union's Mars station refuses an order to grow soldiers for the front.

TIMELINE.arc: A foundry that became a state, and the UN's patron long before it was the UN's navy.
end: UNEL's lunar half

Hardened by its own cold war and the Tranquility Rising, the Republic puts its fleets under the UN and closes the lanes to Earth. Its Assembly becomes UNEL's lunar chamber and its Guard the Luna half of the fleet, and the Custodian gives the lunar bastion its name.
ev: The Rivet Strike: the workers who will crew the Moon arm their Lifters.
The Shackleton Charter: the lunar towns get councils.
Ascension's lunar half merges with the cities: the Lunar Republic.
Applies to join the UN within a week; vetoed, and seated as an observer.
The first Tellus frames go to Geneva as a gift.
The Albedo goes to the fire lines in Provence and Liguria.
The vetoed Geneva Orbital Draft is pinned up in the yard crews' mess.
The Pressure War: Malapert's seal fails, and emergency law follows.
Every bloc's first warships come off the Republic's slipway.
The Custodian rises in the slipway between contracts.
The Earthrise: two prototypes for the white squads' best pilots.
The Tranquility Rising: the Lunar Guard retakes the city.
The Lunar Mandate: the Republic's fleets end the war.

TIMELINE.arc: Vetoed by every bloc, so it starts bringing its own frames.
end: United Nations of Earth and Luna

Given the lunar fleets because every side had let it into the ruins. Its relief agencies become the Office of Global Stewardship; its white squads and the lunar crews become the Directorate of Unified Security.
ev: Leaves New York for Geneva when the flood barriers fail.
Three bloc vetoes; the Non-Aligned states take their case to the Assembly instead.
Asks the blocs to treat mechs as weapons of war. None sign.
The white convoys: borrowed frames, painted white, escort food through the raid zone.
A UN envoy brokers the Aceh truce; Kizunas dig under the UN flag.
A white squad walks the Gran Chaco ceasefire line for a year.
UN footage of H-17's fall reaches every Union parliament.
The Lunar Republic gives the white squads their first Tellus frames.
The Geneva Orbital Draft: vetoed by every bloc, pinned up on the Moon.
Mong Hsat: two white squads destroy the Iron Sawbwa.
The Pact vetoes Herat; the Secretary-General reads out the dead.
The Geneva Address: a standing force, vetoed three times.
The Open Cities: places the war may not enter.
The Lunar Republic puts its fleets under the UN.

TIMELINE.arc: Mercenaries, the recorded dead and a silent giant, acting where governments won't.
end: Communion and the Celestial Prosperity Syndicate
Communion begins with the polar refugees, its faith found later in the cold. Vireo's continuity contracts become part of the Syndicate houses' capital.
ev: The Kivu Contracts: the firm that becomes Grey Lantern.
Vireo starts recording dying patients' minds.
Grey Lantern's Lantern Customs, built from stolen parts.
The Choir: eleven dead pilots who vote on every action.
The Choir holds the bridge at Herat for nine hours.
Vireo sells continuity contracts to families in orbit.
Grey Lantern's counterfeit Concord goes up for hire.
The Polar Exodus; a silent giant walks with the refugees.
The Makassar Fire: Vireo's hidden halls burn, and nobody knows what got out.
A lone frame digs a village out of a Sulawesi landslide and walks into the forest.
Beijing charters the prospecting houses at Juno.

ACE_ERAS: Nobody had written the doctrine yet, so the first aces wrote it: whoever survived long enough to explain what had worked.
The Forty-Minute War made every bloc's aces famous for the same thing: time. Kestrels raced their batteries, and everyone else learned to wait them out.
Svalbard, the Hari River and the Great Sand Sea. The blocs started building frames for named pilots, and pilots for named frames.
Prototypes, test ranges and the first warships. Most of the famous pilots of 2186 are famous for what they might do.

fr: Issue M4 with an M30 and bolt-on ATGM tubes.

Brannock-Hale's answer to the Mindanao Garrisons, which sank to the knees in jungle mud. Longer legs, feet half again as wide, nine tonnes of armour taken off and the GT-900 derated for the heat. It walked out of mud an M4 drowned in, and a single shoulder-fired rocket could stop it. Eight were built; the Army took the M9's redesign instead, which is why the designations skip from M6 to M9.
ACES.k: 7 tanks and 2 vehicles in eleven minutes
ACES.x: Led the four Garrisons down the ravine at Iron Gate. His frame fired first and scored most. The Army made him its first mech ace under a definition it wrote that week: five armoured kills in a frame. He later ran the Longstride's jungle trials in the Philippines.
ACES.z: Took a reserve commission under the Partnership Act and spent twenty years teaching Teamster crews at a Brannock-Hale depot. His Garrison stands outside the gate.

fr: One of the dozen built, with the tethered LR-1.

The airframe that proved the two-second transformation: a Merlin's wings and nacelles on a Sparrowhawk's legs, before the quick-swap battery spine existed. Its fixed pack gave it twenty-two minutes in the air, which is why the production HX-7 was redesigned around swappable batteries. Three were built.
ACES.x: Led the Merlin flight at the Battle of the Talysh Mountains. His flight stood off outside the Tieniu's reach and took the column apart with LR-1s: thirty-one rounds for nine kills. One of his wingmen was brought down, and the Mk.I core the Pact recovered came from that frame.
ACES.z: Became Halcyon's chief test pilot and flew the first two-second transformation in an HX-6. He has said in public that he won the battle that day and lost the war.

ACES.x: The Kestrel's first ace, in the Forty-Minute War. She flew drop-and-strike exactly as written and never stayed past thirty-eight minutes on a battery. When Pact advisers taught the defenders to wait out the clock, she was the first to notice, and started landing early to catch them coming for the swap pits.
ACES.z: Led the Kestrel flight at Svalbard in 2179, and was the first of the four shot down as they transformed.

fr: The last Kestrel block, and the one Svalbard caught: a QX-3 high-density pack, enlarged wing stores and a stiffened hip joint. Everything the Harrier would have except the point-defence laser and the extra armour, and those were what it needed.
ACES.x: Raman-Cole's wingman at Svalbard and the only pilot of the flight to come home: she ejected as her Kestrel came apart and spent two days on the ice. Her testimony is why the Harrier became the standard. She flew some of its first combat strikes over the Hari River, in Afghan markings, hunting rocket batteries.
ACES.z: Commands the 1st Harrier Wing. She has not let a flight transform within sight of an enemy since.

fr: Battery crane on one arm, M30 on the other.
ACES.k: 8 frames, every one inside her own pit
ACES.x: The highest-scoring pilot of a support frame in any army. Osprey crews fight when the pit is attacked, which is often, and her pit near Shindand was attacked nineteen times during the Hari River Offensive. She never once left it.
ACES.z: Still a specialist. She has turned down promotion three times because it would take her out of the pit.

fr: An Écuyer rebuilt as a lookout: a telescoping six-metre sensor mast behind the head, a second fuel cell where the left arm's ATGM tubes had been, and nothing else added. It could watch a convoy route for three days without moving. Forty were built for escort screens in Africa, and the line ended at the Maghreb Depot Strikes, when every one of them was grounded for want of hydrogen.
Licence Garrison with the VEK sensor head.
ACES.x: Commanded the Vigie screen that rode with Union-financed copper convoys through militia country in Zambia, beside the mining houses' armoured walkers. He saw the militias' rebuilt Garrisons first, every time, which was the point of the Vigie. He became the Union's first credited ace in a fight he never claimed was fair.
ACES.z: Grounded with the whole Écuyer fleet in the Maghreb Depot Strikes, without a shot fired at him. He helped draft Directive 5: blind first, fight second.

fr: The Ehrlich works' answer to a cavalry screen that walked at a Garrison's pace. Kassel took a third of the armour plate off, re-geared the knees for a running stride and put a second fuel-cell stack where the pile bunker's pump had been, so a Blitz could top a ridge, look over it and be gone before anything turned. The left arm carries the M2 tubes instead of the bunker. The German contingent ran them in pairs ahead of the Union's tank columns, and the crews named them for how fast they came and went. About sixty were built.
ACES.x: Led a Blitz pair in the German contingent's screen. In the Maghreb Depot Strikes the Blitz pairs were the last Écuyers still moving, because the second stack carried three days of hydrogen, and Reuter's pair spent all of it chasing American raiders between the depots. All three kills came in those three days.
ACES.z: Left the screen when the Haubert replaced the Écuyer, and now runs the Ehrlich test range at Kassel, where every VEK leg since has been proven.

fr: The jungle refit of the surplus Écuyers Brazil bought for the Amazon Logging War. Brazil had no hydrogen depots, so the fuel cell runs on hydrogen reformed from sugar-cane ethanol, which every river town sells. Sealed hips and knees for wading, splayed mud feet, a machete blade on the left forearm for cutting a firing lane, and the sensor head re-tuned to find hot engines under the canopy rather than across a plain.
ACES.x: Sent from Lisbon to train the Brazilian squadron that flew the Union's surplus Écuyers, because she spoke the language. She ended up flying with them through the Amazon Logging War and finding frames under the canopy that helicopters had flown straight over.
ACES.z: Stayed in Belém when Strasbourg recalled her in 2180. Brazilian crews still call the jungle kit "the Valadares", and Brazil still buys from Europe and sells to Africa.

fr: The first Falco, built for her. Every Falco starts as a Haubert with a third of its armour removed, Stack-R racing cells and hand-tuned actuators; hers keeps the Destrier's lance mount on the right arm and carries a G35 on the left hip, because she wanted to finish fights rather than snipe them. Red and gold, like all of them.
The only one. A Falco rebuilt around the Lama Ardente plasma blade, with Destrier arm bracing and a licensed capacitor core in the chest. Forty seconds at full power, then nothing but the lance.
ACES.x: The Union's first famous ace. At Svalbard the Pavises jammed a Kestrel flight and shot four as they transformed; Marchetti's red Falco finished the other three before they could get off the ice. Strasbourg made her the face of the Ace Showcase, and Castellani built the Saetta for her. Nobody else has fought in it.
ACES.z: Now Roland's pilot, on the ethics panel's one condition that she may refuse any order. She hasn't needed to yet.

fr: Standard Pavise with the Spiegel coilgun.

The Pavise's predecessor and the Union's first EW frame: a Haubert with the jamming suite in a dorsal hump and a G35 rifle. It could blind a Kestrel flight but couldn't kill one before the batteries were swapped, which is why Directive 8 needed a coilgun and why the Arbalète became the VK-5. Sixty were built; the survivors are training frames.
ACES.k: 4 Kestrels in under a minute; 6 in all
ACES.x: Learned electronic warfare in an Arbalète, and led the Pavise pair at Svalbard. Under Directive 5 she jammed the Kestrels' landing approach; under Directive 8 she took the kill shots as they transformed. The press gave Svalbard to the red Falco. The Union staff college teaches it from Brandt's logs.
ACES.z: Runs the hunter-killer lance school. Her students say she has never once mentioned the Falco.

fr: The Polish contingent's Destrier, built at Stalowa Wola: a fifteen-metre lance instead of twelve, a lighter shield, and two tall vanes on the back carrying decoy emitters that the crews call the wings, after the old hussars. It charges faster and draws fire away from the cab, and it loses a slugging match to a standard Destrier. Twelve were built.
ACES.x: Led the Union's "volunteer" lance in the Great Sand Sea War, in desert paint and no national markings, fighting beside the partner-state Falcos. The League factions on the other side learned to shoot at the wings, which is what the wings are for.
ACES.z: Commands Poland's lance school. Her lances train on the plains east of Warsaw, which is where Moscow's siege trains will arrive first.

fr: Calgary's mountain version of the licensed Garrison: shorter snowshoe feet with crampon spikes, a climbing winch on the left arm, and an M30 in place of the heavy gun so the frame could carry its own weight up a slope. The cold-start turbine stayed. Six went to the Caspian, where they were the only frames in either army that could climb the Talysh in January.
ACES.x: A Cree officer from northern Saskatchewan who led the Canadian Tundras sent to the Caspian Crisis. While the Merlins fired from beyond the Tieniu's range, his frames climbed above the column's route and held the pass it had to come back through.
ACES.z: Went to Boreal as a test pilot. The Caribou's week-long idle was his demand: a frame that runs out of fuel on a pass is a monument.

ACES.k: No confirmed kills; 11 Harriers "killed" in exercise
ACES.x: The most famous pilot who has never fought. In a joint Arctic exercise in 2183 she lay in the snow for six days on a reformer-stack trickle, and when a US Harrier wing came over the ridge she scored eleven simulated kills before anyone found her. The Pentagon rewrote its Arctic tactics, and Strasbourg asked for her name.
ACES.z: Born in Montreal, posted in Calgary. Since the Halifax Motion, people keep asking which side of a line nobody has drawn yet she would stand on. She hasn't answered.

fr: Standard Type-01, fired only from a kneel.
ACES.x: In the Pamir Border Clash most Tieniu crews fired standing and were thrown off their feet. Hu read the manual, knelt, and kept hitting. His company copied him within days, and by the second week the whole front had.
ACES.z: Wrote the six-week Tieshan course. Every Pact conscript since has learned to kneel from his drill book.

fr: Standard Type-09 with the long cannon.
ACES.x: Commanded the kneeling line that broke Operation Highland. Her company fired 140 Type-09 rounds that afternoon. The propaganda office put her face on the Tieshan recruiting poster, still the most reproduced picture of a pilot anywhere.
ACES.z: In 2178 Tianshu chose her Tieshan-Kai company for a Spratly reef. She is still there, and Beijing calls it a garrison.

fr: An outrider's Tieniu, stripped by its own crew. The shoulder cannon stays; half the torso armour comes off to make room for fuel drums, water, a stove and a bunk, because outriders live in their frames for weeks between depots. Wider feet for pasture and sand, a herder's radio, and a tow hook on the back, because they don't leave a lame frame behind.
ACES.x: The best-known Steppe outrider. During Operation Highland his crew found the US probe's route a day before Tianshu did, and he took five of its frames from a riverbank the network's maps showed as dry ground. He once towed a lame Tieniu 400 km across the Gobi rather than leave it.
ACES.z: Still scouting the rail lines. Moscow's planners keep a file on him. Tianshu just keeps a weighting.

fr: As far as a Tieshan can be pushed. The Type-09 cannon and its bipod are gone. In their place is a Type-08 carbon blade nearly as long as the frame is tall, on a reinforced right forearm, with a short parrying blade on the left. The multi-fuel diesel is over-governed to drive oversized arm hydraulics, which doubles arm speed and halves engine life. Slab armour is bolted to the chest and thighs, and a dozer-steel guard covers the knee it kneels on under fire. The cockpit is still buried, so the pilot fights by periscope. The legs are unchanged, so a Dao can't turn any faster than a Tieshan; its pilots learn to fight without turning. Regimental depots built it from ordinary Tieshans until Tianlong adopted the kit in 2181.
ACES.k: 17 frames, 12 of them with the blade
ACES.x: A conscript who never left. In the Hari River Offensive his regiment followed the breakthrough groups into the walled villages outside Herat, where a Type-09 couldn't kneel and couldn't miss its own side. His depot cut the cannon off his Tieshan and bolted on a blade, and he fought house to house in it for eleven days. Order 11 ends with blades; Ma is why anyone still takes that part seriously.
ACES.z: Instructs the Pact's blade companies. Tianshu has never once proposed a blade charge, and he has never once waited for it to.

fr: The Air Umbrella's anti-aircraft Tiebi. The Type-09 cannon is removed and the space goes to doubled Type-03 rocket racks, a radar mast that folds into the torso, and a second loader's seat. It can't hold a line against frames any more, so it stands behind one. About two hundred were converted.
ACES.k: 7 aircraft, including the first two Harriers lost in combat
ACES.x: An Air Umbrella pilot in a dug-in Tiebi during the Hari River Offensive. The Air Umbrella is meant to work by mass; Zhou's battery worked by patience, and all seven of his kills came from the same firing position.
ACES.z: Chosen as the Tianyan's trial pilot. He approves about thirty-nine of every forty things Tianshu proposes. Nobody has asked him about the fortieth.

fr: The deniable Medved. No markings, the Grad-M battery removed so it could pass as a defensive frame, and the twin diesels muffled and derated so it could lie up in a wadi for forty minutes without a heat plume. Sold on paper to the Zarqa government. Its forearm cannons were kept, which is all it needed for Kestrels sitting in a swap pit.
ACES.k: 11 Kestrels, most of them on the ground
ACES.x: One of the Pact advisers in the Forty-Minute War, and the one who wrote the lesson down: hide for forty minutes, then hit the swap pits. He led the raids himself, and caught most of his Kestrels with their batteries out.
ACES.z: Commanded the breakthrough groups in the Hari River Offensive. He refused Department Zero's offer to augment his pilots, and was retired the following year.

fr: Standard Volk, flown as it was meant to be: by an augmented pilot.

Department Zero's first frame for augmented pilots and the Volk's prototype: a Medved with its armour cut in half, one diesel removed and the control limits lifted. It turned like nothing else on the range and killed two of its first four pilots. The Volk is what OKB-7 built once it knew which pilots could survive the Rys.
ACES.x: The wolf the observers saw at the Hari River. Western analysts first assumed the Volk was remote-controlled, because no pilot they knew of could survive its turns. Department Zero's could; Voronova was one of the two who had already survived the Rys.
ACES.z: Leads the Staya, six Volks rebuilt to hunt giants. Their first quarry is Morevna, who came through Department Zero in the same intake.

fr: Standard Mamont with the integral maul arm.
ACES.x: The breakthrough groups' best gap-opener at the Hari River. His Mamont went first, drew the fire and opened the line for the Tieshan waves behind it.
ACES.z: Volunteered for the Pamir trials. His radiation dose is a state secret. Since last spring, so is his health.

fr: One half of the first Ashvin pair.
ACES.x: One of the first Indian officers in the breakthrough groups after the Delhi Accession. When the augmented pilots were ordered to transfer to Department Zero, she refused, and wrote the Nashik Oath with the others who did.
ACES.z: Flies one half of the first Ashvin pair. Captain Imran Qureshi flies the other; he signed the Oath the same night.

ACES.x: Japan's first mech hero was a rescuer. Ōmine worked a Kizuna through nineteen days of the 2167 Nankai earthquake and tsunami and pulled 412 people out of collapsed buildings. The JSDF lists him with its aces. His frame has never carried a weapon.
ACES.z: Taught balance control to the first Hayate pilots. His rule was that a frame that can't hold a child can't hold a coastline.

ACES.sv: JSDF · coastal defence, then live test units
fr: Standard Hayate with the HF-1 blade.
ACES.x: Came ashore through the surf on Yonaguni in the JSDF's first mech combat, and finished the Yaeyama Incidents with five kills, two of them with the blade. Japan made no accusations, and neither has she. She was on duty at Tsukuyomi the night of the Raijin Break-in.
ACES.z: The Raijin's test pilot. She was offered shrine training for Takemikazuchi, and declined.

fr: A raid band's Haboob. The Tieniu shoulder cannon and its kneeling brace are cut away, and the space goes to fuel bladders, a second radio and a long-range water tank, so the frame can cross 600 km of desert without a depot. It fights with a hand-held Type-07 instead. It can no longer take on a frame head-on; it was never meant to.
ACES.x: The "father of dust" led the most successful band of the Convoy Raids: disperse, hide, strike, vanish. He hit US, Union and Pact convoys in the same month until foreign presence cost more than it was worth, which makes him one of the League's founders whether Khartoum likes it or not.
ACES.z: Never accepted Protect First. The keepers say his people were at the Kafila Ambush. Khartoum says it was bandits.

ACES.sv: Tunisian army, a Union partner, then the Charter
fr: One of the first Falcos Castellani built in Tunis for a partner state's ace. On top of the usual Falco changes it has the Mistral line's sealed joints and sand filters, Stack-R cells re-tuned to run in desert heat at a shorter service life, and a second sensor on a short mast, because in open desert whoever sees first wins. Red and gold, like all of them.
ACES.x: Flew an early Mistral escorting Union-partner convoys through the Convoy Raids. Abu Ghubar's band made up a song about her, and not a kind one. In the Great Sand Sea War she flew a Falco built for her in Tunis, beside Lisowska's unmarked Destriers.
ACES.z: Went with the Tunis Works when the Maghreb signed the Khartoum Charter. She is the Elissa's test pilot, and the reason its cab has room for a medic.

fr: A Mixed Battalion Sirocco up-gunned in a Khartoum workshop: a refurbished Type-01Q shoulder cannon on mining-rig dampers, so it can fire standing, and a second Q-Mix filter pack. It hits like a Tieniu and walks like a Sirocco, and it needs twice the maintenance of either.
ACES.x: Fought for Khartoum's side in the Great Sand Sea War, the side the Gulf associates didn't bankroll. Her lance met the Jinn twice. The second time she lowered her gun.
ACES.z: Spent a month in the Great Sand Sea with Qadira's designers, watching how the Jinn moves among people. She is the Harmattan's lead pilot.

fr: Her own work frame, armed for the strike. Two RD-9 rivet drivers and a PT-4 torch are welded to the upper arms, the lower arms keep their grapples, and a sheet of hull plate is bolted over the cab. It still can't fight anything that shoots back from range; in a docking spine, nothing can.
ACES.x: Held the docking spine for the month of the Rivet Strike. She disabled five security pods by riveting their thrusters shut, and killed nobody, which is part of why Ascension could afford to settle.
ACES.z: Never handed her Lifter back. Her daughter and two grandsons crew the lunar yard, where a Lifter armed for trouble is still called a teague.

ACES.sv: Ascension station security, then the Republic's
fr: Standard Rigger Security, spike driver and harpoon.
ACES.k: 2 frames disabled; the first fight won in orbit
ACES.x: Station security at the Tether Incident, two years after the Republic took the stations over. He reached the drifting pod third, after the two blocs' boarding teams had already killed three people over it, harpooned both of the frames still fighting and held the pod until it could be towed in.
ACES.z: The Republic's first Marlinspike instructor. Nobody yet knows how a Marlinspike should fight, so he is writing it down as he goes.

fr: A salvage Rigger refitted for a family tender. The cab is pressurised and doubled so two can live in it for a week, a second TH-2 tether harpoon goes on the left arm, and the solar wings are enlarged for long shifts past the elevator. It has no weapons the houses would call weapons. The second harpoon is for duels.
ACES.x: Her house's champion. Out past the elevator, the prospecting houses settle claim disputes by reputation, and when reputation isn't enough, by a tether duel between salvage frames: first to pin the other's harpoon line wins the rock. She has never lost one, and has never put a hole in anyone's hull.
ACES.z: Her house bought a continuity contract for her grandmother in 2186. Beijing still thinks they are contractors.

fr: A logging walker turned into a convoy escort in a Kitwe mine workshop: boiler steel plated over the cab and hydraulics, a rock breaker for a right arm, and a dump-truck engine in place of the original. It can't outrun anything, so it was built to wait.
A scrapped Garrison she rebuilt in the desert garages with sand filters, a mining crawler's hydraulics and a borrowed Tieniu gun.
ACES.k: 6 militia frames, 2 of them at arm's length
ACES.x: The best of the Copperbelt walker crews, and the one who taught van Reenen to watch the spoil heaps. A walker can't outrun a Garrison, so she waited for them with her engine off and closed before they could turn.
ACES.z: Took her workshop north to the desert garages, and taught the first League crews to rebuild whatever turned up. Most League pilots of her generation learned on a frame she had patched.

fr: Brannock-Hale's civilian-security Garrison, sold to mining companies with the fire control locked and the ATGM mounts removed. In Kivu she unlocked the fire control with a laptop and a week of patience, and fitted a Pact Type-07 because ammunition for it was easier to find in Congo than M30 rounds.
Bought new from Calgary, as Boreal still likes to point out, then desert-kitted: sand filters, a white-and-grey finish, and the snowshoe feet swapped for Garrison-pattern pads.
ACES.x: A Minnesotan of Norwegian family who flew Garrisons for the US Army, and one of the four ex-Army pilots who held the Kivu tin mine for eight months against three militias and were paid in ore. The firm renamed itself Grey Lantern the following year.
ACES.z: Runs Grey Lantern's contracts desk. Her rules are still the company's: small teams, the best frame from each bloc, and nobody asks who is paying. She says she had nothing to do with the Raijin Break-in.

fr: Every Lantern Custom is a Kestrel airframe with the transformation removed, a VEK sensor head and an MHI sonic blade. Hers adds a Union G35 she won't explain, armour taken from a Haubert, and a Kestrel battery spine kept in place of the turbine, so it runs silent for forty minutes and then has to stop.
ACES.x: A former Union Haubert pilot from Timișoara. In the Great Sand Sea War she flew for all three sponsors in turn, sometimes in the same month, and never against a team she had flown beside. Before that, she won most of Grey Lantern's fights in the Cabo Delgado gas war.
ACES.z: Grey Lantern's senior pilot. She is said to have been offered the Counterfeit's cab, and to have asked who would be in the other seat.

fr: A depot-sale Sirocco rearmed on both sides at once: a US Hornet pod on the left shoulder and a Pact rocket rack on the right, with two fire-control boxes that don't talk to each other. He fires one side, then the other. Spares for it come from whoever is paying that season.
ACES.x: A Sierra Leonean freelancer with no company and no contract longer than a season. He flew for both sides of the Great Sand Sea War, painted each sponsor's flag on one shoulder, and kept the last one on the other.
ACES.z: Says he'll fight for the Charter when it pays. Khartoum says the Charter doesn't do contracts.

ACES.sv: UN Protection Force · Ghanaian contingent · white convoys
fr: A Technical Refit bought from a Khartoum workshop and rebuilt as an escort: the shoulder cannon swapped for a searchlight mast and smoke launchers, a loudhailer in the head, a dozer blade for clearing roadblocks, and a white finish with a blue head. It kept one 30 mm autocannon, which she fired four times in nine years.

A Zambian mining walker with bolt-on steel plate, bought from the Copperbelt houses when no bloc would lend Geneva a frame. Open cab, no fire control, and a cargo cradle where the demolition boom had been. She drove one for the first six months, before Geneva could afford refits.
ACES.k: 112 convoys through the raid zone; none lost
ACES.x: A Ghanaian transport sergeant seconded to the first white convoys, who drove an armoured mining walker through the Convoy Raids before anyone in Geneva had decided whether she was allowed to. She wrote the escort drills the white squads still use, including the rule that a white frame stops for any convoy that asks, whoever owns it.
ACES.z: Trains white-squad crews in Accra. She says the frame matters less than the paint.

ACES.sv: UN Protection Force · Irish contingent · Gran Chaco observers
fr: A surplus Teamster the United States gave Geneva on condition it never carried American markings again. The rifle mount holds a long-range camera and laser rangefinder instead of an M30, a mast on the shoulder carries a UN beacon, and the feet are widened for the river marshes. It keeps a smoke launcher and a light autocannon for self-defence.
ACES.k: None; a year on the line without a shot fired across it
ACES.x: Led the white squad that walked the Gran Chaco ceasefire line for a year after the Brasília talks. Both armies had second-hand frames and old grudges, and the line ran through the river marshes where the Tieshans had lost and nobody wanted to go back. He walked it every day, on foot as often as in the frame, and filed a report every night that both governments read before their own.
ACES.z: Seconded to Geneva as the Secretary-General's adviser on frame operations. He drafted the standing force the Council vetoed.

ACES.sv: Brazilian Army, then UN Protection Force · commander at Mong Hsat
fr: One of the Hauberts Brazil bought from Europe after the Amazon Logging War, kept on standard hardpoints but rebuilt for the canopy: a sensor head with ground radar, wading seals, and a breaching blade on the left arm. Brazil donated it to Geneva still in jungle green. The white went on over the camouflage, and the green shows through where the paint has worn.
The ex-Union Écuyer she learned on in the Amazon Logging War.

Prototype one of two, refitted after Mong Hsat with the Defender loadout for holding evacuation corridors under fire: layered ceramic-composite plates over the chest, shoulders, arms, hips and legs, a hinged Albedo-pattern visor in place of the dish head, a tall ballistic shelter shield on the left arm with a foot that braces it on the ground, and a heavy lunar coil rifle in place of the carbine. The rectenna folds flat behind the torso in a fight, and the four-person rescue capsule stays. She says it is the first frame she has flown that was built by people who wanted nothing back.
ACES.k: 4 Tieshans at Mong Hsat, the Sawbwa's among them
ACES.x: A Brazilian Army pilot who learned her trade in the Amazon Logging War, in Écuyers that found frames helicopters flew straight over. Seconded to the white squads in 2182, she led two of them up the valley at Mong Hsat and fired the shots that killed the Iron Sawbwa in his own frame. She was the first UN officer to give the order to fire first, and she gave it in Portuguese.
ACES.z: Commands the white squads in the field. Esteves wants her to lead the standing force; while the Council keeps vetoing its funding, she leads the one Geneva can borrow.

fr: A Pact export Tieshan that fought for Bolivia in the Gran Chaco, sold off afterwards and bought by Geneva for the price of its scrap. Rebuilt in Ulaanbaatar with a Garrison's radio, a winterised drive train and a cut-down drum rifle, and painted white. It is the only Tieshan in UN service, which made it very useful at Mong Hsat: the Sawbwa's crews held fire for the half-second it took them to work out whose it was.
ACES.x: A Mongolian lieutenant whose family had scouted for the Pact's frame trains for two generations, and who joined the white squads instead. Her callsign is the Mongolian word for blue. At Mong Hsat she walked her Tieshan up to the Sawbwa's gate in the first light and was through it before anyone fired.
ACES.z: Still in the Shan Hills, where the white squads stayed to clear the jade mines. Her brother scouts for Beijing's frame trains. They write to each other.

ACES.sv: UN Protection Force · New Zealand contingent · lead, the first Tellus squad
fr: One of the twelve the Republic gave Geneva in 2183, flown as delivered apart from the blue head her squad painted on, and a Type-L coil carbine Geneva fitted.
Flown on the 2184 fire lines in Provence and Liguria, cutting breaks ahead of fires the Union's own crews had given up on.
ACES.k: 312 people carried out of Herat in her frame's rescue cradle
ACES.x: A New Zealand Army pilot who led the first squad to fly the Republic's gift. At Herat, while an unknown giant held the Malan Bridge, her Tellus squad worked the riverbank below it, carrying the people who couldn't walk. At Mong Hsat her squad cleared the jade mines' labour camps while Ferraz's took the gate. She is the reason Geneva asked the Republic for an Albedo.
ACES.z: Commands the white squads' Tellus company. She keeps a stone from the Hari River in the cockpit, and her crews have started doing the same wherever they go.

ACES.sv: Lunar Guard, seconded to the UN Protection Force · Earthrise test pilot
fr: Prototype two of two. The cockpit cradle is fitted with a full-body brace, because he can't stand up in Earth's gravity on his own.
The yard militia's Rigger Security he flew on Shackleton's rim before the Pressure War.
ACES.k: No kills. The first lunar-born pilot to fly a frame in Earth's gravity
ACES.x: Born at Shackleton in 2164, one of the first children born on the Moon, and the first lunar-born pilot to stand a frame up in Earth's gravity. He can't stand up in it himself without a brace: the Earthrise's cradle carries him as much as he carries it. He volunteered after the Malapert seal failed, because, he says, the Republic needed someone on Earth's side whom Earth could see.
ACES.z: Flying the Earthrise trials with the white squads in the Atacama. The Farsiders call him a hostage and the Earthward call him an ambassador. He calls himself a test pilot.

ACES.sv: US Army, then mission civilian · Colony One's frame crew
fr: A surplus Army Teamster rebuilt by its own crew for a third of Earth's gravity: half the armour gone, the hybrid plant sealed against dust and fed bottled oxygen, a cab that holds air for two days, and the stake driver kept because it sets bore casings as well as it breaks armour. It is Colony One's only frame.
ACES.k: No kills. Three hurricane seasons holding Gulf seawalls
ACES.x: A Teamster pilot from the stilt towns of the drowned Gulf coast, who spent her Army years on flood duty, holding seawalls and lifting people off roofs, because that was where the Army sent frames it didn't need elsewhere. When the Red Roster's recruiters came to the stilt towns, she answered all three questions yes. The gene therapy ended her commission, so she resigned the morning she took it and went to Mars as a civilian on the mission's contract, with her frame in the hold.
ACES.z: On Mars, keeping Colony One's frame running and its walls standing. She has read Washington's charter twice, and says it was written by people who have never had to fix what keeps them alive.

ACES.sv: Mexican Army, seconded to the Rio Bravo river commission · frame warden
fr: Built at the line the Rio Bravo Compact gave Brannock-Hale, for the river commission: cannon mounts plated over, a dredging scoop on the right arm, flow gauges strapped to the legs, and the stake driver kept for setting weir piles. The commission's frames wear its seal, not a flag.
ACES.k: No kills. No ruling she enforced was ever appealed with a weapon
ACES.x: A Mexican Army engineer seconded to the river commission, and the frame warden of its lower river. When a ruling cut a district's allotment, she was the one who walked the frame out to close the sluice, in front of the farmers it was closing it on, and stayed to explain the ledger. She signed on for Colony One's first resupply with the forty families because, she says, a colony that only knows rationing will need someone who can close a sluice without starting a war.
ACES.z: On the manifest for the first resupply flight, with the commission's ledgers and a frame stripped for the hold. When Mexico joins the United States in the war she will become an enhanced American citizen whom no law yet covers.

at: The Great Sand Sea, with Khartoum behind them
Kivu, where it began; it sails under a new flag each year

og_asc.sky: The elevators, the solar ring and the stations

og_far.sky: The far-side ice camps, the Moon

CHRONO.x: New York's flood barriers fail, Washington won't pay for new ones, and the UN leaves for Geneva.
Ascension's crew land to a parade, with a forty-hour gap in the log. Two of the four never give another interview.
Washington's allies start paying for its carriers in hydrogen, seabed rights and shipyards, and keep paying for thirty years.
After the Malacca seizures, Japan pays for protection at sea rather than fight for it.
The resource states refuse every bloc. Neutral on paper, a battleground in practice.
Washington outbids the Union for South American lithium, and Halcyon builds its future on it.
Four Garrisons come down a ravine in the Zagros and destroy a tank column in eleven minutes: the first mech battle.
Congress hands frame design, building and crew training to Brannock-Hale and Halcyon.
The Union builds it as the Écuyer; Boreal builds it in Calgary as the Tundra, on Washington's terms.
Mining houses bolt plate onto construction walkers to escort copper through militia country: the first mechs outside any army.
Tieniu crews thrown off their feet by their own guns learn to kneel, and the Pact's drill book is born.
Tianlong's scheduler for the frame trains: the first time the Pact lets software decide where its frames go.
The UN asks every bloc to sign a convention on mechs. None does.
Station workers arm their Lifters and hold a station for a month. Ascension settles, and never quite disarms them.
Raid bands from the Horn cross the Arabian Sea on the monsoon, dosed with pirated spacer therapies. India has no frames to meet them.
Japan meets mechs as rescuers: nineteen days digging out the Nankai earthquake.
Turkey closes the Bosporus to frames, and the Pact builds ground-effect craft on the Caspian instead.
Merlins win at Talysh from beyond the Tieniu's reach, and the Pact steals the LR-1 plans anyway.
Undeclared American strikes blind and ground the Union's fleet in two weeks.
A kneeling Tieniu on a ridge India claimed, and India backs down.
The Union writes down what the Maghreb taught it: blind the enemy first, then fight.
Blitz crews who refused to give up their frames squat a hangar at Tempelhof and register as a cooperative.
Four ex-Army pilots hold a tin mine for eight months, are paid in ore, and become Grey Lantern.
Union money funds a Geneva institute learning to grow giant tissue from samples it bought, or stole.
Kestrels introduce drop-and-strike, and Pact advisers teach the defenders to wait out the battery.
India buys export frames from Beijing, and learns to wait on Tianshu's schedule for spares.
An American probe breaks on the Fortress Belt, and no bloc has tried it since.
Ascension gives its lunar towns elected councils, because the Moon is only a mining camp.
Vireo has spent years recording dying patients' minds. In 2174 the first one starts to run.
OKB-7's institute begins neural-interface trials on volunteers who are not always volunteers.
Monsoon bands burn India's largest oil port while its Tieshans wait for parts.
Japan's first mech combat, against frames nobody claims.
Desert raid bands make foreign presence cost more than it is worth, and every bloc leaves.
Darkhan's rail sheds build the fast frames Tianlong wouldn't, for the Steppe outriders.
Montreal sells to the Union at three times Washington's price.
The African states band together on armed neutrality, with Gulf associates.
Borrowed frames, painted white, escort food through the raid zone.
Washington forbids Britain a Union frame, and Halcyon threatens its Kestrel support.
Tianshu chooses a reef in the South China Sea for a Tieshan-Kai company. Beijing calls it a garrison.
A Union lance jams a Kestrel flight and shoots it apart as it transforms. The Union has its first famous ace.
The Pact pushes into western Afghanistan, and observers see the augmented Volk.
A sealed laboratory in high orbit loses contact for nine hours. Ascension blames a solar flare.
Raid frames that move like something alive burn the Ratnagiri fuel depot in forty minutes.
Massed anti-air racks over the Fortress Belt, aimed by Tianshu.
India joins the Pact as a junior partner, and OKB-7 opens a line at Nashik.
Department Zero seals a pilot in a capsule and makes their nerves the control system.
A fusion reactor too big for any frame, steadied only by a shrine-trained pilot.
A giant run by the recordings of eleven dead pilots, who vote on every action.
A thorium reactor on four flatcars feeds the dug-in Tiebis by cable. Nobody on the train runs it; Tianshu does.
Its lunar half becomes the Lunar Republic, which takes the ring and the stations and is seated as a UN observer. The blocs divide the elevators, and Washington takes the Mars mission.
The Mars mission recruits people who already know how to go without.
Someone goes for Japan's beam-weapon frame. The one captured works for Grey Lantern.
Beijing feeds Japan through a bad harvest, and Tianshu starts scheduling its ports.
The Union secretly sends Halden's H-17 in, and loses it. A League mechanic finds the Jinn.
The Republic gives the white squads their first frames, white from the foundry.
Asked to plan a two-front war, Beijing's network names Moscow as the second front.
Two blocs' boarding teams fight over a drifting cargo pod: the first combat deaths in orbit.
A treaty to keep orbit unarmed, vetoed by every bloc and pinned up on the Moon.
The first frame built for space combat, for the catapults of the first warships. Nobody knows yet how it should fight.
The United States shows the world a super robot in public, and every hidden program speeds up.
A seal fails at Malapert, a Speaker is shot, and the Republic answers with emergency law.
Two white squads destroy a warlord nobody else was allowed to touch, and fire first.
A 61 to 39 vote takes Berlin's money. The thirty-nine percent take their drawings to Mongolia.
Biological purity becomes regulation. Forty-one members of Congress vote against it and write a charter for Mars that Washington shelves.
Canada asks for observer status in the Union, and Mexico signs the Monterrey Accords with Washington.
Both sides start stocking a line nobody has drawn.
Britain is refused a slipway at Hampton Roads and asks Strasbourg instead.
Every Union program goes before a panel that can stop it. Roland is the only super it approves.
The League promises to fight for something, the Maghreb joins, and the Union's council can't agree how to answer.
Khartoum's first designed frame, built to shelter people rather than hold ground.
Old raiders steal four cultures of the Jinn's healing tissue.
A frame photographed twice at Ras Hafun, a week apart. Between the pictures its wound has closed.
Beijing demands Department Zero be shut down. Moscow refuses, Delhi backs Moscow, and the Pact splits behind a General Staff that exists only on paper.
Moscow gathers siege mortars and a 50 m shape on the flatcars. Some of the people asking why work in Beijing.
Indian pilots refuse Department Zero and swear that augmentation is equipment, never consumption.
A Koschei pilot cuts the command link and walks north. Moscow sends the Staya after her.
Tianshu drafts the plans and runs the reactors. The Tianyan's pilot approves; the Jingwei's officer can't override.
Berlin's splinter and Darkhan's sheds build the fastest frame anyone has made, and publish the drawings in three languages.
Beijing's customs hold Japanese capacitors, and Mitsurugi copies its archives to Vladivostok and Ohio.
Japan elects a government on a promise to settle with Beijing.
An unknown giant holds the Malan Bridge for nine hours. The Pact vetoes Geneva's resolution, and the Secretary-General reads out the dead.
The Secretary-General names the coming war and asks for a standing force. It is vetoed three times.
Every bloc's first warships come off the Republic's slipway, while each builds its own way up.
In the slipway, between contracts, the Republic raises a giant its books list as a yard tug.
Two prototypes for the white squads' best, on beamed power from the Republic's relays.
The first permanent settlement on another planet, led by one of the two Ares crew who never talked.
Mexican water engineers sign on for Colony One's first resupply, with forty families and their ledgers.
Months later, a lander in Ascension's old livery comes down in Valles Marineris.
After a third bad harvest, the elevators' new owners sell passage up and run a lottery for those who can't pay.
Tianlong's prospecting families keep their own books and buy continuity contracts for their elders.
Beijing charters the Belt houses instead of disciplining them, and a clerk names them the Celestial Prosperity Syndicate.
A lone frame digs a village out of a landslide above Makassar and walks into the forest. Nobody was in the cab.
Grey Lantern's super, built from Concord parts nobody can trace, goes up for hire by the week.
A sealed Arctic frame two people can live in for a month. Ottawa and Washington both claim it.
Central Asia, where both railways meet, becomes the front. The Tian Shan Rail sits on the line.
The Steppe splits between Beijing's protection and the Belt. The wind riders ride the last launches up.
Beijing leases its Belt ships to the Syndicate for the duration. Nobody ever closes the lease.
Canada splits at the Manitoba–Ontario line, and Canadians fight Canadians across the Shield.
A million people carried north onto the ice.
Mexico joins, Central America is taken, and the country becomes the United States of the Americas.
Moscow's siege trains turn west while the Union's council is still voting.
The council orders its Mars station to grow soldiers for the front. The station refuses, and the panel backs Mars.
Japan falls into China's sphere, and Mitsurugi's exiles leave through Vladivostok and Ohio.
Chinese landings spread from the Spratly reef to Indonesia, and American carriers fall back on Australia.
An unclaimed raid burns Vireo's hidden halls under the pump works. Nobody knows what got out.
The League fights as the African Union, and grafting becomes how it keeps anyone alive.
Europeans and Americans go south to the Charter.
The first war between ships. At Yernon one British dreadnought breaks the Russian inner fleet.
Farsiders seize a lunar city; the Lunar Guard and the Custodian take it back in nine days.
The UN names places the war may not enter, and the white squads hold them.
Every front sends people up, on whatever is flying.
Refugees go to the ice. A few say a giant walked with them and never said a word.
Moscow crosses the Bering Strait, and an atomic exchange destroys Vancouver.
Tangier's collective builds a giant from the North African Front's wreckage, and elects its crew.
The Commonwealth catches the raid cadres at last, and puts them aboard ships for Jupiter.
The Republic puts its fleets under the UN and closes the lanes. Each bloc's road to orbit is rebuilt under inspection, and UNEL is founded.
The Union's ethics panel turns its Mars conditions into a charter for everything beyond the Moon.
Moscow and Delhi give the Nashik pilots the Ark and send them away.
A corporate-backed hard power holding Mexico, Central America and Western Canada.
The Union refounded with Eastern Canada and the North Atlantic, around institutions no member can stall.
An AI-guided techno-state with Japan in its sphere.
A people-first Russia and India that closed Department Zero and kept the Oath.
A preservation-first commonwealth, plural after the Southern Crossing.

CHRONO.t: United Nations of Earth and Luna
CHRONO.x: Humanity's last central institution, with its own navy, seated in Geneva and the Luna Custodian Bastion.
Mars divided: a crushed rebellion surviving as a fleet and a memory, and an American-aligned state that can't fight alone.
An engineered, rationalist state holding two thirds of Mars.
A nomadic market power of the Belt.
A kin-first biotechnological civilisation on Ganymede.
An honour-bound compact on Europa and Io.
A sun faith of the outer dark, carried back by a drifting ship.
